item.title: Colton Herta backs Mexico IndyCar race following Pato O’Ward promoter callout
item.description: Motorsport photo As the IndyCar Series prepares to head overseas for its newly announced international showcase in Barcelona, enthusiasm for taking the American open-wheel championship even further abroad is gathering momentum - especially among the drivers themselves. The prospect of a future IndyCar round in Mexico has long been a hot topic in the paddock, with Arrow McLaren ’s Pato O’Ward, a native of Monterrey, front and center as the sport’s most popular driver. Speaking after the Barcelona race confirmation during the F1 round in Mexico, O'Ward renewed his ongoing frustrations with local stakeholders, noting the promotional roadblocks that have stalled a race in his home country. Having previously flagged a lack of genuine hunger and commitment among regional organizers , O'Ward warned that any prospective event in Mexico would require stakeholders who are genuinely passionate about building the sport rather than simply looking for a quick payday. When asked whether IndyCar could succeed in Mexico despite those promotional hurdles, nine-time IndyCar race winner and current Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta voiced resounding support for the idea, highlighting O'Ward's star power and the unique technical demands of the track. “A thousand percent.” Herta said. “I think it could be just as popular. A big reason for that is Pato and his popularity here. I think the racing would be incredible here. I think it would be very interesting to see what an IndyCar could do around this track. Especially with the curbing and the curb profiles. With the IndyCar you can typically be a lot more aggressive with the curbs than in the Formula 1.” Herta, 26, speaks from a unique vantage point. Though deeply tied to the American open-wheel scene with seven full-time seasons in IndyCar, the California native has spent the season bridging the gap to Europe – competing in Formula 2 with Hitech alongside his role with Cadillac’s F1 program. Fresh off his fifth FP1 appearance in Mexico City, Herta is slated for his sixth Friday practice outing of the year at Interlagos this weekend to attain the final point necessary for his long-pursued FIA Superlicense to race in F1. Reflecting further on the broader international trajectory of open-wheel racing and the newly minted Barcelona date, Herta concluded: “I think it would put on a great show. I think Barcelona is a really cool thing. I think it would be cool if they could follow it up with the race here.” Read Also: ECR prepares for IR-28 transition with in-house Dynisma DMG-1 simulator How Spanish engineering and Alex Palou brought IndyCar to Barcelona To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Blue Jays Respond To Anthony Santander's ‘Violent’ Political Social Media Posts
item.description: TORONTO, ON - MAY 29: Anthony Santander #25 of Toronto Blue Jays puts on his hat as he takes the field against the Athletics in their MLB game at the Rogers Centre on May 29, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Mark Blinch/Getty Images) Getty Images On Thursday, the Toronto Blue Jays reportedly responded to a social media controversy concerning the Instagram page of $92 million slugger Anthony Santander. Santander, who has been recovering from a significant shoulder injury, became the subject of criticism after sharing Instagram posts targeting Islam and the political developments surrounding the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. “The first video, shared from the account ‘@theamericantruthproject,’ claimed that all Muslims elected to office on Tuesday are radicals who want to impose Sharia law in the U.S. Congress,” according to BlogTO’s Marley Dickinson , who included screenshots of the since-deleted post. “The second video featured a Christian minister who described Islam as ‘violent’ and ‘driven by war. The minister went on to say that Islam is not peaceful and that there is ‘no such thing as kind Muslims.’” The posts prompted a wave of reactions from baseball fans. The since-deleted posts have also been circulated by numerous social media accounts , many with disapproving messages for Santander. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Longtime Dodgers Backstop AJ Ellis Joins NL East In New Role Toronto Blue Jays Address Surprising Anthony Santander Instagram Controversy The 31-year-old outfielder has become a source of frustration for Toronto supporters for reasons beyond his availability. Santander signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Blue Jays in January 2025 after establishing himself as one of baseball’s most productive power hitters with the Baltimore Orioles. He made the American League All-Star team in 2024, when he hit 44 home runs and drove in 102 runs. However, his Toronto tenure has been disrupted by injuries. He appeared in just 54 regular-season games in 2025 and did not make a major-league appearance in 2026, despite beginning a rehabilitation assignment with Triple-A Buffalo in September. Shortly after the controversy arose, the Toronto Blue Jays issued a statement distancing themselves from the political messages. “Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark,” a Blue Jays spokesperson said, per Dickinson. “Individual comments do not represent our organization’s values and beliefs.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees’ 25-Year-Old Depth Pitcher Cuts Ties With Team After Major Injury Toronto Blue Jays Face Anthony Santander Question After Blockbuster Contract Decision The sudden controversy, pending some additional details that have yet to arise, could add a wrinkle to the Blue Jays’ complicated outlook on Santander. item.title: Fall Sports Update: Field Hockey Prepares for NCAA Run
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 4: Natalie Freeman #1 of the Penn State Nittany Lions and Sienna Dunn #21 defend against Jordan Byers #20 of the Iowa Hawkeyes during the quarterfinal game of the 2026 Big Ten Field Hockey Tournament at Ohio State University on November 4, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. Iowa defeated Penn State 2-1. (Photo by Kirk Irwin Big Ten/University Images via Getty Images) Field Hockey (12-6) Seven saves by Aby Deverka and a goal each from Cooper Cutchins and Lily Holmes lifted Penn State to a 2-0 upset win over No. 1 Northwestern in the regular season finale. Head coach Hannah Prince defeated a No. 1 ranked team for the first time in her coaching career. The win gave the upstart team a new sense of confidence entering the postseason. Penn State’s Big Ten Tournament run was unfortunately cut short with a 2-1 loss to Iowa in the quarterfinals. On the bright side, the team will have a few extra days to rest before the NCAA Tournament. Penn State is safely on the right side of the bubble and should hear their name called on Sunday’s selection show. Women’s Volleyball (17-5) The women’s volleyball team extended its win streak to five with a 3-1 win over Ohio State and a 3-1 win over No. 11 Purdue. Kennedy Martin had 24 kills, nine digs, and six block assists in the win over Purdue on Saturday afternoon. Emmi Sellman added 12 kills, one ace, one solo block, and three block assists in one of her best performances of the season. The Nittany Lions also added another signature win to their resume as the team vies for a top 16 seed in the NCAA Tournament. Penn State is up to No. 11 in the RPI. Penn State has an important road trip this weekend with a match against No. 19 Minnesota on Friday (7pm on Big Ten Plus) and a match against No. 7 Wisconsin on Sunday (4pm on FS1). Women’s Soccer (9-3-5) The women’s soccer team blew out Indiana 4-0 in the final game of the regular season. Emma Johnson, Ellie Kocher, and Kaelyn Wolfe all scored for the Nittany Lions, and Paige Kalal added two assists. The third Penn State goal was scored as an own goal. This was the first match in conference play where Penn State scored more than two goals, and the Nittany Lions went the entire regular season without allowing more than two goals in any game. Penn State now turns to postseason action. The Nittany Lions will face Purdue in the Big Ten quarterfinals tonight (8pm on Big Ten Plus). The winner will face Wisconsin in the semifinals on Sunday (4pm on BTN). Women’s Hockey (9-3) The women’s hockey team posted back-to-back shutouts in 1-0 and 6-0 wins over RIT last weekend. Abby Stonehouse had a hat trick in Game 2 to lift the Lions to a 6-0 win, and goaltenders Morgan Stickney and Maddy Campbell each recorded a shutout. It was a much-needed two-game sweep in regulation for a team still growing early in the season. Penn State will face Mercyhurst on the road on Friday (6pm) and Saturday (1pm). Abby Stonehouse had a hat trick in Game 2 to lift the Lions to a 6-0 win, and goaltenders Morgan Stickney and Maddy Campbell each recorded a shutout. It was a much-needed two-game sweep in regulation for a team still growing early in the season. Penn State will face Mercyhurst on the road on Friday (6pm) and Saturday (1pm). Men’s Soccer (3-9-3) The men’s soccer team closed out an ugly 2026 season with a 2-0 shutout loss to Maryland. Penn State did not win a single Big Ten game and missed the conference tournament for the second straight season. This was not what the program needed to see after pulling in an NCAA championship coach. Hopefully they can turn things around next year, but the early returns are not good. Women’s Basketball (0-1) The Tanisha Wright era is off to an inauspicious start with a 62-61 loss to Cleveland State on Monday night. Ava Black led the team in points (17), rebounds (10), and assists (5), but her double-double effort was not enough to overcome a poor night shooting. Penn State finished just 21 for 66 (31.8%) from the floor, and despite finishing +4 in rebounding, +4 on turnovers, and +4 on blocks, the Vikings escaped State College with a one-point win. The Nittany Lions will look to right the ship with a game at Cincinnati on Sunday (2pm on ESPN+) and a game at Dayton on Monday (7pm on ESPN+).

item.title: Beyond the arc: How overcoming adversity shaped Emma Risch’s basketball journey
item.description: STORRS, CT - NOVEMBER 09: Emma Risch #12 of the Florida State Seminoles shoots a three point shot during the women's college basketball game between Florida State Seminoles and UConn Huskies on November 9, 2025, at Gampel Pavilion in Storrs, CT. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For Florida State senior guard Emma Risch, basketball has been a journey of perseverance, patience and overcoming adversity. After battling injuries during her first two collegiate seasons at Notre Dame, Risch transferred to Florida State ahead of the 2025-26 season, determined to return to the court and play the game she loves. “I was injured 2 years in a row and it’s just like, being able to accept that and keep on going and keep on trying, a lot of people aren’t able to do that,” Risch said. “And I’m blessed to be able to do that with all the, the injuries that I have had, just being able to stay on the floor, um, and get back on the floor is just what I kind of want to be remembered by.” Risch appeared in just seven games as a freshman and 13 as a sophomore with the Fighting Irish. Although injuries limited her playing time, watching from the sidelines helped her develop a deeper understanding of the game. “Just being able to watch everything and not being thrown into the fire right away, helped with probably my IQ,” Risch said. “I learned a lot of things without having to actually be on the floor. Um, but also just just that adversity piece of it, like going through injury, not playing really my 1st 2 years. Um, and just being able to hit the ground running whenever I was.” During her first season at Florida State, Risch appeared in 27 games, scoring 181 points and averaging 6.7 per game. “Then last year was my 1st school year of actually playing um, college basketball without being injured,” Risch said. “Um, and that was kind of just a year to get back on my feet. And then this year, I would say, is really just the year to actually kind of use, like, do what I know I can do, get back to my old self, um, just have fun playing basketball.” Risch opened her senior season with nine points on three 3-pointers against Merrimack. She followed with three points, two rebounds and a block in Florida State’s 74-63 victory over North Florida. For Risch, confidence as a shooter comes from maintaining a positive mindset. “You missed that shot? Okay, I’m going to make the next one. You can’t just harp on the misses all the time.” As a returning senior, Risch hopes to use her experiences to guide younger teammates through challenges of their own. “The biggest thing that I try to live by is control, what you can control.” Beyond basketball, Risch credits head coach Brooke Wyckoff with emphasizing academics, personal development and the importance of being a good person. “I really appreciate that just the whole caring about you outside, making sure you’re taking care of your academics because those are very important,” s

Um, just the care and that she has for all of us outside of being a player.” After spending much of her early collegiate career sidelined by injuries, Risch is embracing the opportunity to contribute and lead in her final season. Florida State improved to 2-0 following its victory over North Florida. The Seminoles will host Florida A&M on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 2 p.m.

item.title: Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well
item.description: Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process. Bwala made the remarks in a post on his X platform on Thursday, following the controversy surrounding the leadership of the opposition party. He said a political party seeking to govern Nigeria must uphold the principles of due process, equity and justice, accusing the Mark-led executive of disregarding those principles in its emergence. “A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice. “You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well,” he wrote. Bwala further accused the leadership of violating the party’s constitution and guidelines, as well as the Nigerian Constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said the alleged violations amounted to a disregard for Nigerians, accusing the party leadership of assuming that the public could be misled over the circumstances surrounding its emergence. Bwala also took a swipe at individuals lobbying on behalf of the party leadership, suggesting that they were expecting financial rewards. The comments came amid the dispute over the ADC leadership and a court ruling affecting the Mark-led executive committee. The post Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well appeared first on Vanguard News .

The post Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: LIV Golf officially ends after last-ditch funding deal collapses
item.description: LIV Golf has announced that it intends to “transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations”, ending the controversial breakaway tour. The move follows the collapse of a financing deal worth more than £200 million, according to a report in the Financial Times. BC Partners Credit had been lined up as potential backers after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support. However, the firm pulled out of the deal because of an exodus of star players, the Financial Times reported. LIV was forced to apply for chapter 11 bankruptcy, which effectively cancelled playing contracts. Among those to depart were Jon Rahm , Sergio Garcia , Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton, Louis Oosthuizen and Lee Westwood. A statement from LIV on Thursday read: "LIV Golf Incorporated and its affiliates today announced that it intends to transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations. Jon Rahm was one of the high-profile players to leave LIV Golf following the bankruptcy filing (PA Wire) "Since April 2026, the League's leadership team, with the support of its independent directors and advisors, has run a disciplined and thorough process to identify the best, value-maximizing path forward for the company and its stakeholders. "That process produced a proposed recapitalisation transaction contemplated by the company's Restructuring Support Agreement with BC Partners Advisors, the credit business of BC Partners, which the company sought to implement through its voluntary chapter 11 proceedings in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey. “Despite extensive discussions, the relevant parties were ultimately unable to reach a consensual resolution of certain outstanding terms of the transaction contemplated by the RSA. As a result, the RSA has been terminated, and the transaction is not expected to move forward at this time.” The wind-down will bring to a close a tour that had drawn some of golf's best-known names away from the established circuits. The chapter 11 filing in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey was the vehicle through which LIV had sought to implement the recapitalisation with BC Partners Advisors. The proposed deal collapsed after the departure of players including Rahm, Garcia and Oosthuizen, leaving the league without the financing it had pursued over the past seven months.

item.title: Three keys to Northwestern vs. No. 19 Iowa
item.description: EUGENE, OR - OCTOBER 31: Aidan Chiles #0 of the Northwestern Wildcats rushes the ball during a game between the Northwestern Wildcats and Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images After a tough loss at Oregon on Halloween, Northwestern returns home to Ryan Field to face the Hawkeyes. Some of the cracks seen throughout the season resurfaced against the Ducks, raising questions about how the Wildcats will bounce back against No. 19 Iowa in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Northwestern enters the game as a 2.5-point favorite against Iowa, according to DraftKings, despite the Hawkeyes coming off an impressive shutout of then-AP No. 25 Wisconsin. Kickoff is slated for 6:30 p.m. CST on FOX. Here are three keys to Northwestern to remain unbeaten at the new Ryan Field on Saturday: Preventing the long plays It starts at safety. The ‘Cats gave up five plays of 30 yards or more against Oregon. That can’t happen against an Iowa team looking to squeak its way into the playoffs. Yes, they will be operating without star running back Kamari Moulton, but it proved itself last week, shutting out Wisconsin 30-0. Robert Fitzgerald is likely to return from the injury he suffered against Ball State. Furthermore, defensive lineman Brendan Flakes has been cleared to return. He last played in the win over Michigan State, when he blocked the game-saving field goal. The takeaway is simple: Northwestern must prevent explosive plays from Iowa. It will help to have some defensive stars back, but the lockdown, “bend don’t break” defense seen against Indiana and Colorado needs to return now that the personnel is mostly healthy. Being creative and innovative Chip Kelly is an offensive genius. Who else runs a triple stack out of the backfield, the famed wing-T and some CFL-style plays in the same game? When asked about it at his weekly press conference ahead of Iowa, head coach David Braun said, “That’s the type of stuff that makes it so fun working with this staff. I’m sometimes sitting in practice saying, like, what? That’s really hard to defend.” And the ‘Cats had better hope it’s hard to defend. The most explosive play of last week’s game against Oregon, a 64-yard touchdown to Griffin Wilde, came out of that triple-stack formation. Kelly’s creativity and innovation are key to confusing opposing defenses. Confusing defensive backs allows receivers to spring open — a component of this offense’s success. When asked about the offense at Big Ten media day at the start of the season, Wilde said, “We’re going to be fast, physical and explosive. Those three words. We’re going to play fast. Aidan Chiles needs to play I wish I could write a more creative section, but Aidan Chiles must play. Full stop. He’s one of the best quarterbacks in the Big Ten, with Yogi Roth, the color analyst on the last three Northwestern football games on Peacock, called Chiles the “greatest reclamation story in college football this year.” Chiles was listed as questionable on Wednesday’s initial availability report. item.title: Spurs' Mitch Johnson collects milestone win
item.description: San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson reacts during the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Dallas Mavericks, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Dallas. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez) (Julio Cortez/Associated Press) The Spurs' Mitch Johnson quietly reached a career coaching milestone Wednesday night. With the defending Western Conference champions pulling out a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, the 39-year-old Seattle native notched career win No. 100. Befitting Johnson's low-key style, the Spurs made no announcements regarding the achievement. Victor Wembanyama, who posted a career-best 52 points, a career-high 24 rebounds and eight blocks, retrieved the game ball at the end of the contest, not for himself, but to give to give to Johnson in the locker room, Spurs courtside reporter Nate Ryan reported via X on Thursday morning. Johnson became the Spurs acting head coach in November 2024 after Hall of Famer Gregg Popovich suffered a stroke. After Johnson guided the Spurs to a 32-45 record, the club named him head coach in May 2025 after Popovich announced his retirement from coaching. The Spurs finished 62-20 last season before starting this season 6-2. Johnson guided the young team all the way to the NBA Finals where they lost in five games to the New York Knicks. The league office confirmed in July 2025 the 77 games Johnson coached in 2024-25 in the wake of Popovich's stroke would go toward Johnson's career ledger. Popovich is the winningest coach in NBA history with a 1,390-824 mark. Johnson was one of the three finalists for NBA coach of the year last season. "To see the growth he's had," the Spurs' Devin Vassell said last April, "to see where he is at now, to be able to come in after a coach like coach Pop, one of the greatest coaches of all time, if not the greatest coach of all time, and have the type of season he's had and be able to lead us and take control over this team and over this organization has been huge to see." item.title: Erling Haaland makes Manchester City demands after narrow Champions League win
item.description: Erling Haaland believes Manchester City 'need to step up a bit' -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images Erling Haaland has called on Manchester City to raise their game if they want to compete for silverware this season. The Citizens narrowly defeated RB Leipzig 3-2 in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, with Haaland proving to be the decisive factor after the hosts had twice leveled the score. Enzo Maresca's squad once again showed defensive vulnerabilities, while Gianluigi Donnarumma was caught off guard for RB Leipzig's opening goal. Nevertheless, City demonstrated resilience to fight back and secure the three points, propelling them into the top eight of the League Phase standings. All the Phil Parkinson questions you wanted to know but were afraid to ask Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid -Credit:DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images Despite the positive result, Haaland is demanding more from his teammates. "I think we need to step up a bit, when we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that," he said, speaking to TNT Sports, via the Manchester Evening News . When pressed on what areas required improvement, the Norwegian forward added: "Keeping the ball, when to keep it when to go, working together offensively and defensively. You can always be better and there's always a new chance. A new game in three days so that's lovely." City return to Premier League action this weekend when they visit Nottingham Forest on Saturday. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE The fixture will mark a homecoming to the City Ground for Elliot Anderson, who made the switch to City during the summer transfer window, and Haaland has been full of praise for how the midfielder has adapted seamlessly at the Etihad, including providing the assist for his decisive goal in Leipzig. "He has been amazing, he has had an amazing start to his City career and that is what you expect," said Haaland. "You have to come straight in and perform. It is not easy to come in, you need to adapt and new players and a new coach, so he he has been impressive. Respect."

item.title: 'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it'
item.description: Jodie Burrage has represented Great Britain at the Billie Jean King Cup [Reuters] After struggling with her blood pressure as she lost her first WTA Tour singles match for 16 months, Jodie Burrage checked in with three things: a doctor, a physiotherapist, and her phone. On her social media feed there were already messages promising punishment - and others making threats on her life - for losing 3-6 6-3 7-5 to Indian wildcard Vaishnavi Adkar. "I try not to actually read what they say," Burrage told BBC Sport from Chennai, where she is still competing in the doubles. "Because we are so used to it - which is really quite sad - I don't fear for my safety. "You've got to have thick skin. There was some brutal stuff that was said, but I don't take it to heart. "Sometimes it hurts more than others. If you've already got other stuff going on, or you're not in a great place, and that is put on top of everything else - this tour is tricky enough as it is." Burrage, who says her blood pressure "tanked" towards the end of the match, decided to share screenshots of the abuse on Instagram to raise awareness of an everyday problem for professional players. "It happens every match - whether it's win or lose," the 27-year-old Briton said. "Playing in Wrexham [on the World Tennis Tour last month], I won three matches [and] lost one. But after every single match there was some sort of abuse. "I think that's where tennis players get it pretty hard - because in tennis you can bet on so many things." Abuse of players, particularly by angry gamblers, is not a new problem. Burrage's compatriot Katie Boulter shared with the BBC last year the abuse and death threats she received on a near-daily basis. This year's WTA and World Tennis report into online abuse, which was based on data from the Signify Group's Threat Matrix service, said "angry gamblers" were responsible for 42% of all verified abuse detected during the 2025 season. It is why there is so much disquiet about the sponsorship deals some tournaments have struck with gambling firms. The Davis Cup, for example, has an official sports betting partner, while in August self-described "prediction-market platform" Kalshi signed a multi-year deal with the US Open. Burrage believes social media platforms "should do more to help". "I think an ID should be put on every Instagram account, and then that way it makes more people more accountable for their actions on that platform," she said. "I think it would limit what people would say. People should be accountable for what they say and that's where I think there could be more of a push to change. "It's only getting worse." All WTA and World Tennis players have access to Threat Matrix's services, which monitor all social media posts directed at players. The first aim is to provide a rapid assessment of whether an individual's safety is under threat. They can then alert the platforms, and potentially law enforcement agencies, to the offending content. Names can also be shared

Burrage, who says her blood pressure "tanked" towards the end of the match, decided to share screenshots of the abuse on Instagram to raise awareness of an everyday problem for professional players. But after every single match there was some sort of abuse. "I think that's where tennis players get it pretty hard - because in tennis you can bet on so many things." Abuse of players, particularly by angry gamblers, is not a new problem. Burrage's compatriot Katie Boulter shared with the BBC last year the abuse and death threats she received on a near-daily basis. The Davis Cup, for example, has an official sports betting partner, while in August self-described "prediction-market platform" Kalshi signed a multi-year deal with the US Open. "I think an ID should be put on every Instagram account, and then that way it makes more people more accountable for their actions on that platform," she said. "I think it would limit what people would say. People should be accountable for what they say and that's where I think there could be more of a push to change. "It's only getting worse." All WTA and World Tennis players have access to Threat Matrix's services, which monitor all social media posts directed at players. The first aim is to provide a rapid assessment of whether an individual's safety is under threat. They can then alert the platforms, and potentially law enforcement agencies, to the offending content. Names can also be shared with gaming companies, so they have the option of banning offenders from their platforms. The service can extend to direct messages and even the moderation of accounts, so players never see the message in the first place. But this is not foolproof - and players may feel they would rather know about any threats made against them. Burrage has recently been able to improve her singles ranking to 474, from a low of 888 in July. Injury prevented her playing singles for nine months and when she returned for the grass court season, sickness held her back. But she will not allow the abuse to throw her off course. "I'm at a place where it's all bigger picture for me and everything I'm doing now is to have a good season in 2027," she added. "I'm building a team that is really good around me. They know where I've been, what I've gone through. "It's not what you want, but if I have to go through it, then I will." item.title: Falcons Eye Cheap Help With Kayshon Boutte Trade Talk
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons sit at 3-5 after a brutal shutout loss to Tampa Bay, but they are not out of the NFC South race yet. That reality has sparked a fresh trade idea that could bring wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the city. ESPN analyst Seth Walder identified the Houston Texans receiver as the affordable help Atlanta needs before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Boutte arrived in Houston from New England back in August, yet his time there has been rough. He has caught just 15 passes for 194 yards with no touchdowns in seven games this season. His numbers were much better with the Patriots last year, when he posted 33 catches for 551 yards and six scores. Now the Texans have added Marvin Harrison Jr. and fallen to a 2-5 record, which might make them willing to listen to offers. A Second Move for Boutte Walder sees a clear path for this deal to happen despite the recent history. In his Nov. 4 trade deadline preview, he highlighted the unique situation surrounding the 24-year-old receiver. “This would be the second time Boutte has been traded this season, after the Patriots dealt him to Houston in August,” Walder wrote, according to Heavy.com . On Aug. 24, New England received safety Jaylen Reed plus a 2028 seventh-round pick so the Texans could acquire Boutte. Following Jayden Higgins’ season-ending knee injury, Houston needed depth, and the arrival of Harrison Jr. changed its roster needs. “But that was before the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. (and before the Texans got out to a 2-5 start),” Walder added. With a new star at the position, Boutte might be expendable for a struggling Houston team. Why Atlanta Makes Sense The Falcons have invested in receivers like Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus this offseason, but the production behind Drake London has been uneven. With 39 catches totaling 624 yards, London tops the roster, but the depth chart misses a dependable second choice. Walder believes Atlanta’s spot in the division makes this affordable addition worth the risk. “The Falcons are 3-5 but not out of the race in the NFC South, so adding a cheap player who could help is not out of the question, and Boutte is exactly that,” Walder wrote. The receiver is in the final year of his rookie contract, which carries a 2026 cap charge of about $3.7 million, so the Falcons face minimal financial risk. This trade remains a recommendation from Walder rather than a confirmed report that talks have started. The Falcons face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8, and they need to decide if they can improve their offense before the deadline.

item.title: Penn State vs Chattanooga Preview: Second Tune-Up Before Pitt
item.description: Penn State basketball's Roko Prkacin (8) shouts after dunking the basketball vs. Canisius on Nov. 2, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Who: Chattanooga Mocs When: Thursday, November 5, 6:00 PM EST Network: Big Ten Network Kenpom Ranking (Penn State): 253 (87) Line: PSU -12.5 Penn State opened the season on Monday with a rout of Canisius. The Lions got a late bump from the availability of Roko Prkačin, who went for 28 points in his debut as a Nittany Lion. Their second game of the season is against a Chattanooga that should pose no threat before the real test begins. The Chattanooga Mocs, coached by former Penn State player Dan Earl, has a roster make-up not too dissimilar to the Lions, with three overseas players, two D2 players, and a litany of other transfers making up the 17-man roster, to go along with the six players that returned. They hung around with Louisville in the second half of their opener, but the hole they had to dig out of was too big to overcome. Chattanooga approached their roster makeup the same way Penn State did. Get old, by any means necessary. Many players have played big minutes against grown men or carried teams at other levels. The challenge is that almost none of them have played together. Tonight is only their second game as a group. So both the Mocs and the Nittany Lions are going into a game where the majority of the players are playing their second game as a team. Scouting the Opposition The Mocs shoot a lot of threes. Against Louisville, 33 of their 57 shots came from three. They made 12 of them, for 36.4%. Four players made at least two threes. That includes Yonatan Levy, a 6-10 forward who stretches the floor. Chattanooga took few free throws and made only 57.1% of them. On defense, they forced 10 turnovers and got eight steals. They did not control the glass. Louisville had 17 offensive rebounds. Lenny Anigbata and Zach Bleshoy, a forward and guard respectively, were the other players alongside Levy to have a double-digit outing against the Cardinals. What to Watch For Pressure – Can Penn State’s pressure create turnovers early, the way Louisville’s did? The Mocs committed 18 turnovers against Louisville, so Penn State can take advantage. Rebounding – The Mocs were terrible on the glass last time out, so this shouldn’t be much of an issue for the Lions. Moc Shooting – Chattanooga is going to shoot threes. They’re going to make a good chunk of them. Can the Lions stop them from making too many of them? Prediction It probably won’t be the laugher that Canisius was, but Penn State should still come out ahead. Penn State 88, Chattanooga 78

item.description: ‘Greatest Sports Show Ever,’ ‘They Still Got Their Fastball’ — NBA Fans in Stitches Over Charles Barkley’s Savage 2-Word Comeback to Shaquille O’Neal Despite earning millions of dollars and earning awards, praise, and kudos as players, Charles Barkley and Shaquille O’Neal earned a new following. As two of the analysts on “Inside the NBA,” Barkley and O’Neal have worked together since the 2011-12 season. In analyzing the modern game, the legends bring an elite player’s viewpoint to the show. More importantly to many, the duo engages in a rare banter filled with barbs, jokes, and levity that makes many viewers smile. Recently, Barkley engaged in a small back-and-forth that drew a strong reaction from fans. Social Media Explodes with Laughter Over “Inside the NBA” Segment Barkley and O’Neal have a long history on and off the court. They were both selected to the Western Conference All-Star roster in 1997, although neither played because of injury. As opponents, they’ve competed 19 times, with O’Neal winning 11 of those matchups. The duo even engaged in a brawl on the court. However, as a pair, they will be best known for their work together on “Inside the NBA”. The honor drew criticism online because of Patel’s controversial tenure as FBI director. For example, after the United States Olympic men’s hockey team won the gold medal at the 2026 Olympics, Patel’s appearance in the locker room drew criticism for his judgment and his use of government resources during the trip to Italy. Barkley ventures a little further . “He’s not available right now,” he said. The midterm elections took place Tuesday, with Democrats seizing control of both the House and Senate. Democrats quickly signaled plans to use subpoenas and investigations to scrutinize members of the Trump administration and its allies. Patel has been under scrutiny for months. Barkley seemed to suggest that the FBI director is conferring with legal counsel. Meanwhile, what stands out most about the Barkley/O’Neal relationship is its influence on the show’s structure . “Greatest sports show ever,” one user tweeted. Host Ernie Johnson serves as a de facto traffic policeman, keeping the show moving quickly and ensuring the laughs are balanced by actual analysis. Two-time NBA champion Kenny Smith, while he offers humor, presents himself more as a hands-on analyst. item.title: Is the Lockout Coming? — The Complete MLB Offseason Preview
item.description: Last Wednesday, the marathon was completed. Fans checked in for Spring Training in February, celebrated Opening Day in March, built a love-hate relationship with their team all summer, and then watched the Milwaukee Brewers win their first-ever World Series in October. Now, it’s time to start the process all over again. But that process will look a lot different this winter. In fact, this may be the most important offseason in Major League Baseball’s 150-year history. Here’s everything you need to know as we head into this apprehensive, monumental offseason. The Impending Lockout On the morning of Dec. 2, baseball will shut down. For the first time in 32 years, baseball is attempting to implement a salary cap. It has never been enforced, making MLB the only sports league in North America without one. The current Collective Bargaining Agreement expires at midnight on Dec. 1. The CBA is baseball’s sole governing contract and determines everything from player contract structures to postseason format. It expires and is renewed every half-decade or so. Immediately after Dec. 1, Major League Baseball, represented by all 30 team owners, league executives and club officials, will inflict a lockout. This will freeze everything from free agent signings to access to club facilities. The purpose is leverage. The league is pushing the MLB Players Association to agree to a new salary cap (and floor) system , and it will not be pretty. View this post on Instagram The last time the owners pressed for a cap, it almost killed baseball entirely. It happened during the 1994 season, when the players unhesitatingly disagreed and went on strike . It lasted 232 days, from August to April and canceled a World Series. This was very detrimental to the sport. The strike cost baseball the fans’ support and trust, and once it returned, it was never the same. Stadium attendance and TV viewership plummeted. It even played a key role in the death of the Montreal Expos, who had a winning club in ‘94 but imploded thereafter. And now it’s time to do it all over again. The big question this time is how long it will last. There’s a grave chance it affects the 2027 season, with real potential for missed games. That said, clubs have one month to sign free agents without being affected. Free Agent Market Buckle up for the next 28 days. With the uncertainty of how long the lockout will last, teams will be aggressive in November while they can. Like this offseason, the free agent class is also unusual. Many players’ agents have avoided ending contracts right now in fear of the lockout, so few superstar, franchise-altering players are up for grabs. However, there is one: two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal . He’s been the premier starting pitcher for the last three seasons and won consecutive AL Cy Youngs in 2024 and 2025. item.content:encoded: Last Wednesday, the marathon was completed. Fans checked in for Spring Training in February, celebrated Opening Day in March, built a love-hate relationship with their team all summer, and then watched the Milwaukee Brewers win their first-ever World Series in October. Now, it’s time to start the process all over again. But that process will look a lot different this winter. In fact, this may be the most important offseason in Major League Baseball’s 150-year history. Here’s everything you need to know as we head into this apprehensive, monumental offseason. The Impending Lockout On the morning of Dec. 2, baseball will shut down. For the first time in 32 years, baseball is attempting to implement a salary cap. It has never been enforced, making MLB the only sports league in North America without one. The current Collective Bargaining Agreement expires at midnight on Dec. 1. The CBA is baseball’s sole governing contract and determines everything from player contract structures to postseason format. It expires and is renewed every half-decade or so. Immediately after Dec. 1, Major League Baseball, represented by all 30 team owners, league executives and club officials, will inflict a lockout. This will freeze everything from free agent signings to access to club facilities. The purpose is leverage. The league is pushing the MLB Players Association to agree to a new salary cap (and floor) system , and it will not be pretty. View this post on Instagram The last time the owners pressed for a cap, it almost killed baseball entirely. It happened during the 1994 season, when the players unhesitatingly disagreed and went on strike . It lasted 232 days, from August to April and canceled a World Series. This was very detrimental to the sport. The strike cost baseball the fans’ support and trust, and once it returned, it was never the same. Stadium attendance and TV viewership plummeted. It even played a key role in the death of the Montreal Expos, who had a winning club in ‘94 but imploded thereafter. And now it’s time to do it all over again. The big question this time is how long it will last. There’s a grave chance it affects the 2027 season, with real potential for missed games. That said, clubs have one month to sign free agents without being affected. Free Agent Market Buckle up for the next 28 days. With the uncertainty of how long the lockout will last, teams will be aggressive in November while they can. Like this offseason, the free agent class is also unusual. Many players’ agents have avoided ending contracts right now in fear of the lockout, so few superstar, franchise-altering players are up for grabs. However, there is one: two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal . He’s been the premier starting pitcher for the last three seasons and won consecutive AL Cy Youngs in 2024 and 2025. If he signs before the lockout, Skubal could become the highest-paid pitcher of all time. Skubal leads the starting pitchers, the strongest group in this free-agent class. Other notable names include Michael King , Freddy Peralta , Sonny Gray and new Japanese transfer, Kaima Taira . Taira is one of three star players coming from Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball league. He has a career 1.78 ERA in his eight years with the Saitama Seibu Lions. Taira’s market will be lively, but a different Japanese slugger is the prize asset. Meet Teruaki Sato , a 27-year-old power-hitting third baseman. Sato is a five-time NPB All-Star, won the 2025 Central League MVP and is coming off a Triple Crown season. View this post on Instagram Because of the smaller market, Sato may be the best hitter available. The other best bats available include Seiya Suzuki , Luis Arraez , Randy Arozarena , Jake Bauers and Jazz Chisholm Jr. Adrian Morejon and David Bednar highlight the reliever market. However, Bednar, among eight other players, received qualifying offers from their clubs to return for one more season. Of the players aforementioned, Suzuki, Arozarena, Bauers, Morejon and Bednar all have until Nov. 17 to accept or decline. A Winter To Remember Some rumors around the league are starting to permeate. That said, expect a flurry of deals to begin by the second week of November. As of Nov. 3 , four clubs seem to be invested in Skubal. The Los Angeles Dodgers, who traded for him at the 2026 Trade Deadline, the New York Mets, Chicago Cubs and New York Yankees. While the Mets and Dodgers have the checkbooks to rule, don’t sleep on the Cubs. A lot of pieces from Chicago’s rotation are hitting free agency, and Skubal could be a great band-aid – and an expensive one at that. View this post on Instagram A few trade speculations have begun, too. The Tampa Bay Rays could seek to deal starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen , since his final year under contract is 2027. If a free agent, Rasmussen would be at the top of many teams’ lists. Reports also suggest the Baltimore Orioles could open shop after another disappointing season. They may have begun the overhaul at August’s Trade Deadline, sending catcher Adley Rutschman to the Boston Red Sox. A Ketel Marte trade is also up for real discussion. Marte’s relationship with the Arizona Diamondbacks severely weakened in 2026, and the club even began entertaining a trade last year. Through all the entertaining rumors of player movement, the undeniable defining feature right now is the lockout. Whether an agreement comes sooner than expected or lasts well into 2027, this offseason will be historic. Major League Baseball is at a climax. The sport is actively competing with the National Basketball Association for engagement, something that hasn’t happened in decades. International attention is growing, and the sport as a whole is thriving. The future of baseball will be decided in a couple of months, and we’ll all get a front-row seat. The post Is the Lockout Coming? — The Complete MLB Offseason Preview appeared first on The Lead .

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz Reaches Paris Masters Quarterfinals After Matteo Berrettini’s Withdrawal
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz advances to the quarterfinals of the ATP Masters 1000 in Paris after Matteo Berrettini withdrew from their scheduled third-round match due to an arm injury. The Spaniard has now matched his best career result at the Paris Masters, having previously reached the quarterfinals in 2022. Berrettini Withdraws Ahead of Third-Round Clash Berrettini’s withdrawal brings an unfortunate end to his campaign in the French capital. The Italian had enjoyed a promising start to the tournament, defeating Brandon Nakashima 6-4 3-6 7-6 in the opening round. He followed that result with a 7-6 7-5 victory over Ugo Humbert to reach the third round. Berrettini was set to face Alcaraz in what promised to be an interesting encounter at the Paris Masters. However, the 2021 Wimbledon finalist announced his withdrawal shortly, citing persistent pain in his arm that had been bothering him for several days. Berrettini explained through social media that the discomfort would prevent him from competing and that he would undergo medical examinations in the coming days to determine the extent of the injury. Alcaraz Matches His Best Result in Paris Alcaraz has also had a positive start to his campaign, defeating American Alex Michelsen 7-6 6-3 in his opening match. The 23-year-old, who received a first-round bye as one of the tournament’s top seed, has now reached the Paris Masters quarterfinal for the second time. He previously achieved the same result in 2022, although his run ended in the last eight after retiring during the match against Holger Rune due to an abdominal injury. Despite his success on the ATP Tour, the former World No. 1 is still chasing his first semifinal appearance in Paris. He will have the opportunity to do so when he faces either Arthur Fils or Taylor Fritz. Mar 22, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Carlos Alcaraz (ESP) reaches for a forehand against Sebastian Korda (USA) (not pictured) on day six of the 2026 Miami Open at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Fils and Fritz Battle To Take on Alcaraz Arthur Fils will take on Taylor Fritz in Thursday night session, with the winner advancing to face Alcaraz. The Frenchman is bidding to become the first player from his country to reach six ATP Masters 1000 quarterfinals in a single season. Already qualified for the ATP Finals in Turin, Fils will also be looking to continue his impressive campaign on home soil. Fils reached the third round after defeating Tomas Machac 6-3 7-6, having received a first round bye. Meanwhile, Fritz enters the encounter with additional pressure. The American is currently 11th in the Race to Turin and still has a chance to qualify for the ATP Finals. A victory over Fils would set up a quarterfinal encounter with Alcaraz. If the American manages to defeat both and reach the semifinals he will be moving closer to securing a spot in Turin. With a place in the semifinals at stake, Alcaraz will be looking to maintain his momentum and make the most of his

item.title: Vikings announce huge Carson Wentz decision for Week 9 vs. Bills
item.description: Vikings announce huge Carson Wentz decision for Week 9 vs. Bills originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After their first loss of the season, the Minnesota Vikings sit at 6-1. Following their loss to the Detroit Lions , the Vikings are set to face the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. As the NFL trade deadline is right around the corner, the Vikings will look to get back in the win column against one of the best teams in the NFL. It won't be easy, especially since the Vikings are making a big change. Thanks to Kyler Murray's hamstring injury, the Vikings, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , have made the decision to start Carson Wentz on Monday Night against the Bills. Vikings to start Carson Wentz vs. Bills as Kyler Murray deals with hamstring injury "Just in: Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game vs. the Buffalo Bills while Kyler Murray deals with what the team has called a 'sore hamstring'," Schefter reports. Kevin O'Connell told reporters this news Thursday, the team's first day of practice leading up to Week 9 against the Bills on Monday Night Football. Facing a shaky Bills defense, the Vikings will hand the keys to the offense over to Wentz as Murray deals with this hamstring injury. It's not likely a lengthy absence for Murray, as it's only a week-to-week issue, but if Wentz impresses, the Vikings might stick with the former Philadelphia Eagles and Indianapolis Colts QB for the foreseeable future. MORE : 4 stats that show how bad Chargers' Justin Herbert has been in 2026 The Vikings got a chance to see Wentz early this season, as he went 2-0 as the starter against the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears , albeit in some odd game scripts, coming in after Murray's Week 1 injury, and in Week 2 during a rainy, close game. But now, Wentz has a real chance to start in primetime. A strong outing, and he might convince O'Connell to stick with him as the starting QB. Murray is not going to start for Minnesota this week as he deals with a hamstring injury, but with his lackluster production so far, Wentz has a real chance to steal this starting job. He is the Week 9 starter, but there's a non-zero chance he keeps the gig going forward. item.title: Minnesota Vikings Make Major Quarterback Decision Following Loss to Detroit Lions
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings suffered their first loss of the 2026 season against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, and now they’re reportedly making a significant change at quarterback. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell says Carson Wentz will start Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills , while Kyler Murray continues dealing with a hamstring injury sustained during Minnesota’s 19-15 loss at Ford Field. The development gives Wentz another opportunity to lead the Vikings, who entered last Sunday’s game undefeated before running into a determined Detroit defense. Sep 27, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz (11) warms up during the first half against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. item.content:encoded: The Minnesota Vikings suffered their first loss of the 2026 season against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, and now they’re reportedly making a significant change at quarterback. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell says Carson Wentz will start Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills , while Kyler Murray continues dealing with a hamstring injury sustained during Minnesota’s 19-15 loss at Ford Field. The development gives Wentz another opportunity to lead the Vikings, who entered last Sunday’s game undefeated before running into a determined Detroit defense. item.title: Falcons’ Brian Robinson Jr. gets injury update ahead of Bengals game
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Falcons’ Brian Robinson Jr. gets injury update ahead of Bengals game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Falcons will be facing the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid this week as they look to get the bad taste out of their mouth from their game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offense was not up to par, and it started with Michael Penix Jr., who finished the game with four interceptions . With the weather conditions, it may have been better for the Falcons to just run the ball, but Bijan Robinson didn’t have the success they needed. For the past few weeks, Brian Robinson Jr. has been sidelined because of a hamstring injury, and it’s safe to say that has played a part in the running game not being that effective as well. The good news for the Falcons is that Brian is practicing this week, and he was limited in their recent session , according to D. Orlando Ledbetter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Falcons injury report. RB Brian Robinson Jr. was limited,” Ledbetter wrote on X, formerly Twitter. If the Falcons can get Brian back, that would be big for the run, as they’ve made it an emphasis to get that area of the offense rolling before anything else. The Falcons could be without one of their speedsters this week, as rookie Zachariah Branch didn’t practice because of a hamstring injury. It’ll be interesting to see if he’s able to practice tomorrow, because if not, there’s a good chance he doesn’t play. As for the defense, the Falcons are set to get James Pearce Jr. back on the field after he served his eight-game suspension. That should give the defense a boost, putting more pressure on the quarterback, with this week being Joe Burrow. Billy Bowman Jr. was also a full participant in practice after missing time with a hamstring injury. It looks like the Falcons are getting healthy at the right time as they try to stay in the mix of the NFC South. Related: Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. completes 8-game suspension, officially eligible for Bengals matchup Related: Falcons’ Kevin Stefanski already rules 2 players out for Week 9 clash with Bengals

item.title: ‘It’s disappointing’: Rob Gronkowski addresses video connecting him to Turning Point USA
item.description: Credit: Turning Point USA, Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports New England Patriots legend and Fox Sports NFL analyst Rob Gronkowski is addressing a photo that many thought indicated his political beliefs. The former tight end was spotted near a Turning Point USA tent on Election Day, Tuesday. Turning Point USA is an American nonprofit organization that advocates for conservative politics and was founded by the late Charlie Kirk in 2012; it is now headed by his widow, Erika Kirk. Gronkowski, who was with his girlfriend Camille Kostek in New Hampshire, was waving an American flag near a Turning Point USA tent on Tuesday, leading many to believe that he was there supporting the organization and conservative politics. However, that isn’t the case. “It doesn’t matter what party you’re voting for. It’s just important that you go out there and vote,” Gronkowski said, via The Mirror. “It has been upsetting and eye-opening to see the narratives around my visit to NH on Election Day with Camille,” he posted. “In regard to the images and videos circulating, we are not endorsed by or affiliated with Turning Point USA. Gronk stiff-arms Turning Point USA https://t.co/7X8PUcHajL — Peter Hamby (@PeterHamby) November 5, 2026 “After stopping at Goffstown High School, we crossed the street to greet excited fans yelling out our names before leaving to the next location. We simply took some pictures, and I signed some things for them before leaving. “We took photos with people across the political spectrum throughout that morning. We cannot control what the media has made of it and running with – so we are here to shut down the false narratives. “It’s disappointing to see an innocent moment stripped of context and turned into clickbait. Our message has always been and always will be to treat everyone with kindness and hope you all will do the same.” Gronkowski’s heralded NFL career saw him win four Super Bowl titles, accumulate four All-Pro selections, while finishing sixth in all-time receiving yards for a tight end with 9,286 and third in career touchdowns with 92. The post ‘It’s disappointing’: Rob Gronkowski addresses video connecting him to Turning Point USA appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Mike Vrabel Slams $138M Trade Rumors Over Barmore And Davis
item.description: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Head coach Mike Vrabel says he has not told anyone that two of his biggest stars are up for grabs. Vrabel pushed back hard on Wednesday, Nov. 4, questioning where these stories even started. He called the rumors “drummed up” during a press conference; his team had earlier beaten the Miami Dolphins 24-19. The speculation comes from Sports Illustrated insider Albert Breer, who said New England has already held talks with other clubs. Breer told Boston.com that the team could move Barmore for a fourth-round pick. He also noted that the Patriots want to develop younger players and fix their money issues. This suggests the front office may try to trade members of their $138 million defensive duo before the Nov. 10 deadline. Vrabel Denies the Talks Vrabel did not rule out a trade entirely, but he made it clear he did not start the rumor mill. NBC Sports Boston’s Phil Perry shared the coach’s direct response on X. “I have not shared that information with anybody. This time of year, I think all these things get drummed up… I don’t know where a lot of these things come from,” Vrabel said. The coach appears annoyed that people think he is trading his own players without his permission. The team sits at 5-3 after that win over Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1. They face the Green Bay Packers next on Sunday, Nov. 8, at Gillette Stadium. Six days remain until the trade window closes. The Cost of Moving Stars Breer indicated that Barmore is “very clearly available” for the right price. If the Patriots do decide to sell high, they might get a mid-round pick in return. However, losing a star like Barmore or Davis would hurt the defense right when they need to stop the run and cover big receivers. The team has 20 players on injured reserve this season, so depth is already thin. Other outlets like the Boston Herald and Musket Fire have discussed what the team needs most. Some say they need a running back or an edge defender more than they need to trade away talent. The Patriots have three outside linebackers on their 53-man roster, which is a small number for a team trying to win. If they trade a key defender now, they might have to spend more draft capital to fill the hole later. Vrabel’s comments on Wednesday suggest he wants to keep control of the narrative. He is waiting to see if the offers are worth giving up a player who knows the system. The clock is ticking down to Nov. 10, and the front office has to decide if a fourth-round pick is enough to lose a starter.

item.title: Updating Florida's top 10 football recruits after Brysen Wright reclassifies
item.description: The class of 2027 just added one of the nation's premier wide receivers. Mandarin five-star wide receiver Brysen Wright has recommitted to the 2027 class. Wright was ranked the nation's No. 1 in the 2028 class by USA Today. The 6-foot-3½, 215-pound Wright is a human highlight reel who seemingly makes multiple jaw-dropping plays each week . The Mustangs use Wright in all three phases, but he projects as a prototypical outside wide receiver at the next level. Through the regular season, Wright has caught 46 passes for 984 yards and 11 touchdowns, and rushed two times for 92 yards and a touchdown. Defensively, Wright has 26 tackles, a tackle for loss, two interceptions, three passes defended, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery. With Wright reclassifying to the 2027 class, here's an updated USA Today Florida top 10. 10. Wyatt Smith, St. Thomas Aquinas Height, weight: 6-6, 235 pounds Position: Edge Verbal commitment: Ohio State 9. Fred Ards III, Jones Height, weight: 6-5, 225 pounds Position: Edge Verbal commitment: Texas A&M 8. Aaryn Washington. item.title: Vikings have made quarterback decision for Monday Night Football vs. Bills
item.description: It didn’t take long for speculation to morph into a confirmation on the Vikings quarterback front. A few hours after Adam Schefter hinted that Minnesota was trending toward starting Carson Wentz at quarterback against the Bills in Week 9 as normal starter Kyler nurses a hamstring injury, we know now that will in fact be the case: Just in: Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start Monday night’s game vs. the Buffalo Bills while Kyler Murray deals with what the team has called a “sore hamstring.” pic.twitter.com/YM6AR24m9q — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 5, 2026 Murray’s injury was suffered last week against the Lions. And he wasn’t playing particularly outstanding football this season to date. Wentz threw three touchdowns in Week 1’s win over the Packers after Murray got hurt while scrambling early in the game. Now the Bills won’t have to guess which quarterback they’ll see inside U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis on Monday night. It’ll be Wentz.

item.title: Time to panic? Tyson Fury has ‘some injury’ which ‘may stop him’ from boxing Anthony Joshua on Netflix
item.description: RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA - DECEMBER 21: Tyson Fury reacts to the judge's points decision after his bout with Oleksandr Usyk at Kingdom Arena on December 21, 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Mark Robinson/Getty Images). | Getty Images Former champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, two of the biggest names in heavyweight boxing over the last decade, are currently scheduled to collide atop a Netflix-streamed fight card on Fri., Dec. 11, 2026 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. But former WBC heavyweight titleholder Frank Bruno claims Fury suffered an undisclosed injury, which may be severe enough to cancel the fight. “I looked at him the other day, and I think someone was talking to me in the gym that he’s got some injury, which may stop him from going into the fight with Joshua,” Bruno told Tony Bellow . “And having that on your head ain’t nice.” If “The Gypsy King” is indeed injured, don’t be surprised to see one of these titans replace him. Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) ended his second retirement layoff to stop Polish ham and egger Mariusz Wach last July in Thailand . Similarly, Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) bounced back from a horrific car wreck overseas to put the hurt on Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia just a few months back . For more boxing news and notes click here .

item.title: UNC spent a shocking amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi
item.description: UNC spent a shocking amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . North Carolina football has endured a whirlwind campaign in Bill Belichick's second season in charge. The famed football coach has the Tar Heels on the brink of a potentially qualifying for a bowl game — a welcome sight after a dour 4-8 season last year. Off-the-field, though, things are far more murky. The 74-year-old has been without two of his closest confidants for much of the season. Belichick's son and defensive coordinator, Steve, and North Carolina's general manager, Michael Lombardi, left their posts early in the year amid an internal investigation into alleged wrongdoing among figures in the program. On Thursday, it was revealed just how much the Tar Heels spent to look into the program's affairs. Suffice to say, it was a princely sum. With that, here's a look at the final price tag for UNC's investigation. MORE: Inside UNC's internal investigation into allegations of drug use and sex among players, staff UNC spent extortionate amount of money on investigation involving Steve Belichick, Michael Lombardi WRAL's Brian Murphy reported that North Carolina shelled out nearly $1 million to look into the program's affairs in the fall. The investigation, first reported by WRAL , unearthed several concerning allegations, including claims of improper sexual relationships and drug use within football facilities. Lombardi and the younger Belichick were key figures in the inquiry. Both handed in letters of resignations after the findings of the inquest were made public. The investigation found that "certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina's values and standards of conduct." Importantly, the probe did not deem these actions to be systemic. Lombardi stepped away from the program on Sept. 3, hours after the Tar Heels played in their season opener. He had been placed on paid administrative leave since late July after being made the subject of a human resources complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. Steve Belichick announced his intention to resign two weeks later. He only recently formally stepped away from his post; his resignation wasn't tendered until Oct. 27, as he had previously been placed on medical leave. He had been placed on paid administrative leave since late July after being made the subject of a human resources complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. Steve Belichick announced his intention to resign two weeks later. He only recently formally stepped away from his post; his resignation wasn't tendered until Oct. 27, as he had previously been placed on medical leave. item.title: The Colts are making a big mistake by delaying their trades
item.description: (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are in their fire sale and rebuilding era. While the team has been agonizingly close to being competitive in the past, success has routinely been fleeting in the Shane Steichen era, leaving him as one of the most vulnerable head coaches in the NFL when it comes to guessing who will be fired next. For a while it appeared as though the Colts were all aboard the rebuild train, after trading All-Pro offensive guard Quentin Nelson to the Seahawks and sending DeForest Buckner to the 49ers a day later — but now the team might be pumping the brakes on any more deals for a few days. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the belief around the league is that the Colts have essentially hit pause on trade conversations and are choosing to play through the weekend, with an eye on dealing their biggest assets on Monday or Tuesday ahead of the trade deadline. This is a move to try and squeeze as much juice out of their assets as possible, but it’s also a gamble that could backfire. Indianapolis has three primary assets teams are looking to trade for: RB Jonathan Taylor, WR Josh Downs, and DT Grover Stewart. While a handful of other players could be dealt, those are really the three names making noise right now. Taylor is the crown jewel of the market. If we look at the state of the league, there are a few teams that make the most sense: The Vikings, in dire need of an offense; the Seahawks, with a running attack that needs to be bolstered; and the Patriots, who need to take some pressure off Drake Maye being the bulk of the offense. Minnesota is in a great spot at 6-1 atop the NFC North but feels like the team with the least gas to continue a run. Right now might be the best possible time to make a deal with the Vikings, giving them the offensive ammunition they so desperately need in order to compete with the Bills on Monday Night Football . item.content:encoded: (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are in their fire sale and rebuilding era. While the team has been agonizingly close to being competitive in the past, success has routinely been fleeting in the Shane Steichen era, leaving him as one of the most vulnerable head coaches in the NFL when it comes to guessing who will be fired next. For a while it appeared as though the Colts were all aboard the rebuild train, after trading All-Pro offensive guard Quentin Nelson to the Seahawks and sending DeForest Buckner to the 49ers a day later — but now the team might be pumping the brakes on any more deals for a few days. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the belief around the league is that the Colts have essentially hit pause on trade conversations and are choosing to play through the weekend, with an eye on dealing their biggest assets on Monday or Tuesday ahead of the trade deadline. This is a move to try and squeeze as much juice out of their assets as possible, but it’s also a gamble that could backfire. Indianapolis has three primary assets teams are looking to trade for: RB Jonathan Taylor, WR Josh Downs, and DT Grover Stewart. While a handful of other players could be dealt, those are really the three names making noise right now. Taylor is the crown jewel of the market. If we look at the state of the league, there are a few teams that make the most sense: The Vikings, in dire need of an offense; the Seahawks, with a running attack that needs to be bolstered; and the Patriots, who need to take some pressure off Drake Maye being the bulk of the offense. Minnesota is in a great spot at 6-1 atop the NFC North but feels like the team with the least gas to continue a run. Right now might be the best possible time to make a deal with the Vikings, giving them the offensive ammunition they so desperately need in order to compete with the Bills on Monday Night Football . If the Colts wait there’s a very good chance Minnesota loses to the Bills, falls to 6-2, slides out of first place in the division, and begins reassessing their chances. While a loss certainly wouldn’t put them out of contention, it might be enough to raise questions about whether or not adding Taylor would be enough to get them over the hump. If that happens, then a good trade return could evaporate. In Seattle, there are going to be questions about whether or not the juice is worth the squeeze as well. This team already made a trade with the Colts to bolster their line, so double-dipping and adding a running back might be too rich for their blood. This team should be able to win easily over the Cardinals on Sunday, but that would get them to 5-4. This is an extremely good football team, but the way the NFC is breaking, it appears that both Wild Card spots will go to the NFC North, and there’s not a lot the Seahawks can do to change that. In the NFC West, the 49ers are in a great spot to win the division, with the Rams trying to make inroads. It’s a hard sell to let the games play out on Sunday, and if the 49ers, Rams, and Seahawks all win — then it’s increasingly difficult to buy the idea that Seattle needs to trade multiple picks to try and catch a 7-1 team in San Francisco. When it comes to New England, they sit in a very similar position to the Seahawks. It’s just unclear if they have the juice to make a serious run this season, and with a tough game against the Packers on Sunday, the result of that game could determine if the Pats fall to 5-4. There’s so much competition for the Wild Card spots in the AFC that, again, this team could have a little more foresight and decide that parting with picks just before the deadline just isn’t worth it. If reports are to be believed, and the lack of action in Indianapolis suggests they are, then it appears the Colts are in holding mode. The issue is that the longer they wait, the more likely it becomes that these player-needy teams will look in other directions or reassess the direction of their season. A nightmare scenario for Indianapolis would be to wait too long, see the most desperate teams bow out of discussion, and be forced to trade Taylor to someone like the 49ers, who are wily enough to offer a lesser trade packages the Colts are hoping for, knowing they’re in sell mode. To a lesser extent, these same scenarios are also happening with Josh Downs and Grover Stewart. Simply put: There is a gulf emerging in the NFL between the best teams in the league, and those who are already looking ahead to 2027. This is not a great year to find a division leader who truly believes they’re “one piece away,” or find a team desperate enough to make a truly foolish deal (like the Colts did last season with their Hail Mary trade for Sauce Gardner). Front offices work on the idea of promise and imagination. The more games you allow to take place before making a deal, the more teams have clarity about what their situation actually is. This is a “bird in the hand” moment for the Colts, and they truly might regret not getting these deals done now, instead of holding through the weekend.

item.title: WTA Apologizes for ‘Failing’ to Tell Players About Mics After Jessica Pegula Is Caught Criticizing Mirra Andreeva
item.description: Jessica Pegula; Mirra Andreeva Credit: Matthew Stockman/Getty; Lintao Zhang/Getty NEED TO KNOW The WTA issued an apology to players and coaches after Jessica Pegula was caught criticizing Mirra Andreeva on a livestream “We sincerely apologize for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed,” the WTA said Pegula was heard calling Andreeva a “diva” and said she “needs to be humbled” The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) has issued an apology for not informing players and coaches that microphones were recording their practices. “The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players’ practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals,” the association said in a statement to Front Office Sports’ Colin Salao on Thursday, Nov. 5. “We sincerely apologize for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed,” the WTA concluded in the statement. The WTA’s apology came one day after American tennis pro Jessica Pegula was caught on a recording criticizing Russian tennis pro Mirra Andreeva . Jessica Pegula on Oct. 14, 2026 Credit: Robert Prange/Getty Pegula, 32, was speaking with her coach after practice for the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, Calif., on Wednesday, Nov. 4, when she called Andreeva, 19, a “diva” and said she “needs to be humbled” and “put in her place.” Pegula also referenced Conchita Martínez, who coaches Andreeva, and said the coach eggs on Andreeva’s behavior. “If I was a coach and my girl, you just played four great games, and you’re up four-zero, and you’re mad at me, hitting balls at me, I would be like, first of all, [that’s] disrespectful to the other person,” Pegula says in the video. “You’re four-zero, shut the f--- ... ” she continued to her coach. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Pegula added, “Conchita, like pokes her and like eggs on her behavior,” and then referenced Coco Gauff — who she’ll face in the Finals on Sunday, Nov. 8. Pegula said if Andreeva had Coco Gauff’s “mentality,” then she would “be better than Coco.” PEOPLE reached out to reps for Pegula, Gauff, Andreeva and the WTA for comment. Read the original article on People
