item.title: MC&J: Week 10 in college football will see Ohio State try and shake off last week’s loss
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) runs back to the line of scrimmage for a two point conversion attempt after scoring a touchdown during the NCAA football game against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Oct. 31, 2026. Ohio State lost 30-18. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Last week ATS: 6-11 (4-4 National, 2-7 B1G) Season ATS: 87-82 (35-35 National, 52-47 B1G) Last week my performance was a lot like Ohio State’s. Uninspired, confusing, frustrating, and anything else you felt while watching the Buckeyes lose to USC. The last few weeks have been rough, as all of the gains we made earlier in the season pretty much erased. This week is a great week to get back on track. Not only are we in a new month, there are a ton of great games on the schedule this Saturday. Hopefully we can kick off November strong and pile up the wins all month long! National games No. 9 BYU v. No. 3 Utah (-4.5) – 12:00 p.m. ET – ABC At first I thought such a high-profile game being played at noon was going to be a FOX broadcast. Not exactly sure why a game of this magnitude is being played at 10 a.m. in Salt Lake City but I guess they had to put it somewhere on a Saturday that is loaded with great games. Maybe ABC/ESPN is trying to punish Utah after they were apparently mean to Pat McAfee a couple weeks ago. Last week looked like a prime letdown spot for Utah after beating Houston. The Utes had no problem with Cincinnati, beating the Bearcats 49-25. Utah was incredibly balanced last week, throwing for 266 yards and rushing for 268 yards in the blowout. If the Utes can replicate that performance each week, in combination with a tough defense, they’ll be a hard out in the College Football Playoff. I’m wondering if BYU might have already peaked this season. The high point was obviously the win over Notre Dame in Provo, but since then the Cougars have lost in overtime at UCF, followed by an unimpressive win over Arizona State. While BYU is a good team, I don’t think they are quite at the level of Utah. Utah 27, BYU 17 No. 2 Georgia (-3.5) v. No. 10 Ole Miss – 7:30 p.m. ET – ABC Georgia will have revenge on their minds when they travel to Oxford on Saturday night. Ole Miss ended the Bulldogs’ season last year, beating them in the Sugar Bowl in the CFP. Kirby Smart’s team enters this game coming off a dominant performance against Florida, only allowing the Gators to score eight points. After getting after Florida’s backup quarterback last week, the Bulldogs will have a tougher task on Saturday night, as they’ll have to try and slow down Trinidad Chambliss. The Rebels had no problem last week with Auburn, beating the Tigers by 30 points. Even without running back Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss still ran for 224 yards. This week will be a lot tougher sledding for the Rebels since they’ll be trying to solve a tough Georgia defense. No. 10 Ole Miss – 7:30 p.m. ET – ABC Georgia will have revenge on their minds when they travel to Oxford on Saturday night. Ole Miss ended the Bulldogs’ season last year, beating them in the Sugar Bowl in the CFP. Kirby Smart’s team enters this game coming off a dominant performance against Florida, only allowing the Gators to score eight points. After getting after Florida’s backup quarterback last week, the Bulldogs will have a tougher task on Saturday night, as they’ll have to try and slow down Trinidad Chambliss. The Rebels had no problem last week with Auburn, beating the Tigers by 30 points. Even without running back Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss still ran for 224 yards. This week will be a lot tougher sledding for the Rebels since they’ll be trying to solve a tough Georgia defense. If the running game can’t get going it will put even more pressure on Chambliss, who will be trying to replicate his magic from the Sugar Bowl. Obviously Georgia is one of the best teams in the country, I’m just not convinced they are a true title contender. Gunner Stockton was pretty pedestrian last week against the Gators, and I’m wondering if the Bulldogs have enough firepower to keep up with Ole Miss if this ends up being a higher scoring game. I’ll ride with the Rebels to spring an upset and add to the chaos in college football this year. Ole Miss 31, Georgia 24 No. 1 Miami (FL) v. No. 11 Notre Dame (-5.5) – 7:30 p.m. ET – NBC There have been a lot of questions about how good Miami is since they have played nobody so far this season, but do we really know how good Notre Dame is? The best win of the season for the Fighting Irish came in the opener against Wisconsin. The one time Notre Dame played a team with a pulse, they lost on the road at BYU. A second loss this season would all but end the playoff hopes for Marcus Freeman’s team. Miami has had some close calls over the last few weeks, but that could work in their favor in this one. Even though their opponents haven’t been very good, the Hurricanes at least have had some experience playing in tight games. If Darian Mensah wants to win the Heisman Trophy this year, Saturday night is the perfect time for him to stake his claim to the award, as a win on the road in South Bend under the lights would be huge. I like the points in this one since I think Miami is the better team. Malachi Toney is going to end up being the difference since he is absolutely electric when he has the football in his hands. Even if Notre Dame ends up winning here, I’m not convinced they do it by at least six points. Miami (FL) 34, Notre Dame 30 B1G games No. 8 UCLA (-5.5) v. Minnesota – 12:00 p.m. ET – FOX UCLA is now just four wins away from an undefeated regular season in Bob Chesney’s first season as head coach. Despite the Bruins losing starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava for the season in the Oregon game, they are still the only team in the Big Ten without a loss. It helps the Bruins haven’t had too tough of a schedule, with games against Wisconsin, Michigan State, and Nevada following the win over the Ducks. Imagine where Minnesota would be at right now if they had even the slightest bit of consistency. It feels like immediately after the Golden Gophers look like they could be a threat then they end up losing. Last week is a perfect example. Following a win over Iowa, Minnesota has Indiana on the ropes but loses to the Hoosiers in overtime. I do like this spot for Minnesota. Getting a west coast team for an early kickoff in Minneapolis. The Golden Gophers have a stout defense that I think could cause some problems for UCLA and their running game. One thing is for sure — if Minnesota wins this week, then it’s probably a lock they lose next week to Penn State. Minnesota 21, UCLA 17 No. 19 Iowa v. Northwestern – 7:30 p.m. ET – FOX Oh what could have been for Northwestern. The Wildcats held a 20-6 lead on Oregon in Eugene in the first half before letting the Ducks off the hook in the second half. Had Northwestern won last week then it would have been time to start talking about the Wildcats possibly being a part of the College Football Playoff. The offense actually did their part against Oregon, it was the defense that let them down. Iowa looked great last week in a 30-0 shutout of Wisconsin. Quarterback Hank Brown was nearly flawless, only missing on four of his passing attempts, finishing with 222 yards and two scores. The Hawkeyes controlled the clock against the Badgers, holding onto the football for 36 minutes in the victory. When Iowa is playing like that then they are nearly impossible to beat. If Iowa does win the rest of their games in the regular season then they would have a strong case to make the CFP, only losing to Ohio State and Minnesota. The remaining schedule for the Hawkeyes isn’t too terribly difficult, so winning out is a definite possibility. Northwestern could have a rough month of November with the Hawkeyes this week, followed by Ohio State next week. Iowa 24, Northwestern 13 No. 23 Oregon v. No. 12 Ohio State (-7.5) – 3:30 p.m. ET – CBS Luke Fahey’s first collegiate start didn’t go exactly as planned. There definitely was a lot of anger being thrown around by Buckeye Nation on Saturday night but Fahey wasn’t the main target. The true freshman wasn’t great but he also wasn’t terrible. The bigger issues were with the coaching staff and the defense. At times it looked like the Ohio State defense had forgotten how to tackle. Oregon also have had to deal with the loss of their starting quarterback, as Dante Moore is out for the season after suffering a concussion against USC. Former Ohio State commit and Nebraska quarterback Dylan Raiola has taken over behind center for the Ducks. Last week Raiola engineered a comeback win against Northwestern, finishing with 336 yards passing and three touchdowns. Ohio State will have to put the ugly

item.title: DeChambeau Faces Uncertainty As LIV Golf Rescue Fails
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images The dream of a revived LIV Golf league hit a hard wall on Wednesday. BC Partners, the private capital firm expected to lead a major restructuring, has pulled its investment bid entirely. This move effectively kills the plan for “LIV 2.0” just as the tour faces a critical bankruptcy hearing. The Financial Times broke the news on Wednesday, reporting that the firm could not secure the necessary player commitments to make the new model work. Without this funding, the breakaway league faces total liquidation. The situation leaves high-profile players like Bryson DeChambeau without a clear tour to play on for the 2027 season. The collapse comes after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund announced it would end its financial backing after the 2026 season, a deal that had seen the fund invest more than $5 billion since the league launched in 2022. The Collapse of the $300 Million Plan BC Partners had been poised to inject up to $300 million into the league to help it emerge from its restructuring. This capital was intended to succeed the Saudi Public Investment Fund as the primary backer. The firm made an initial investment in October and planned to provide the full amount to strengthen finances ahead of the 2027 season. However, the deal fell apart because the firm lacked belief that enough players would commit to the league. The Athletic cited multiple sources to report that LIV Golf is now preparing to wind down operations. A source told talkSPORT that “Essentially, time has run its course” regarding the possibility of reviving the tour with the necessary roster. The deadline to show sufficient player support for a 2027 tournament series had loomed large, and BC Partners decided to drop its bid rather than proceed without guarantees. In September, the league filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, yet stated plans to keep operating during reorganization. That hope is now fading fast. The Financial Times cited people directly familiar with the matter to confirm the decision came as the deadline approached. Reuters received no comment from LIV Golf upon contact, nor did BC Partners reply to comment requests. Player Reactions and the Team Golf Dream The withdrawal of the investor leaves a massive void for the remaining stars. Since the bankruptcy filing, a wave of high-profile golfers, including former world number one Jon Rahm, has already departed LIV. Tyrell Hatton and Ian Poulter have also opted to leave, while Sergio Garcia has returned to the DP World Tour. Bryson DeChambeau, one of the biggest names on the roster, had recently expressed strong support for the league’s future. DeChambeau told Figuring Out with Raj Shamani that he was very excited about the team format. “The point of it is that the team golf stuff, I was very excited about ,” the 33-year-old said. He had previously stated that the business model for the league’s proposed 2.0 era “makes a lot of sense” and that he hoped it would last “forever.” Fol

This capital was intended to succeed the Saudi Public Investment Fund as the primary backer. However, the deal fell apart because the firm lacked belief that enough players would commit to the league. A source told talkSPORT that “Essentially, time has run its course” regarding the possibility of reviving the tour with the necessary roster. The deadline to show sufficient player support for a 2027 tournament series had loomed large, and BC Partners decided to drop its bid rather than proceed without guarantees. In September, the league filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, yet stated plans to keep operating during reorganization. That hope is now fading fast. The Financial Times cited people directly familiar with the matter to confirm the decision came as the deadline approached. Reuters received no comment from LIV Golf upon contact, nor did BC Partners reply to comment requests. Player Reactions and the Team Golf Dream The withdrawal of the investor leaves a massive void for the remaining stars. Since the bankruptcy filing, a wave of high-profile golfers, including former world number one Jon Rahm, has already departed LIV. Tyrell Hatton and Ian Poulter have also opted to leave, while Sergio Garcia has returned to the DP World Tour. Bryson DeChambeau, one of the biggest names on the roster, had recently expressed strong support for the league’s future. DeChambeau told Figuring Out with Raj Shamani that he was very excited about the team format. “The point of it is that the team golf stuff, I was very excited about ,” the 33-year-old said. He had previously stated that the business model for the league’s proposed 2.0 era “makes a lot of sense” and that he hoped it would last “forever.” Following a recent interview where he seemed to commit his future to the tour, DeChambeau might now face limbo. While The Athletic reported that roughly 30 players are believed to have signed for the upcoming season, the financial backing required to run the league has vanished. Critics have long argued against the league’s impact on the traditional game. What Comes Next for the League The immediate future involves a legal process that could end the league’s existence. LIV is anticipated to appear at a hearing scheduled for Thursday in the US bankruptcy court located in Trenton, New Jersey. This meeting could start the liquidation process. As the situation unravels, The tour spokesperson signaled a lack of clear communication by failing to return The Athletic’s call when approached for comment. BC Partners backed out before decisions were made, or at least before they were revealed to the public. The firm determined it had exhausted the time available to make the “LIV 2.0” concept viable. With the Saudi funding ending after 2026 and the private capital now withdrawn, the league has no clear path forward to host a tournament series. The financial gap left by the $300 million investment is too large to fill without the player support that never materialized. The next scheduled event is the bankruptcy hearing on Thursday in Trenton, New Jersey. This date marks a potential turning point where the court could order the dissolution of the company. Until that hearing concludes, the status of the remaining players and the league’s assets remains uncertain. The failure of this rescue plan ends the chapter on the ambitious attempt to restructure LIV Golf as a sustainable competitor to the PGA Tour.

item.title: Peter Rosenberg ‘scammed’ by Kimberley A. Martin behind the scenes at ESPN
item.description: Credit: ESPN, ESPN New York Everything was fine between Peter Rosenberg and Kimberley A. Martin until one of them tried to sell popcorn to the other. Rosenberg and Martin were on First Take Wednesday morning. And in the afternoon, Martin joined Rosenberg’s ESPN New York radio show with Don La Greca and Alan Hahn. During the radio appearance, Martin joked about Rosenberg being a “diva” on First Take earlier in the day, which prompted Rosenberg to accuse Martin of holding him up for $50. But even while accusing Martin of holding him up for $50, he didn’t realize he was being scammed by his ESPN colleague. Despite being longtime colleagues, Wednesday was the first time Rosenberg and Martin met in person. And upon meeting, Martin told Rosenberg about a popcorn fundraiser for her daughter. ﻿ “I did lie,” Martin admitted on the radio. “I said it was my child. It’s not my child, I don’t have any children.” Martin’s admission stunned Rosenberg, who interjected her recap of the $50 popcorn sale to ask, “You were literally lying?” “Oh, did we not talk about that?” Martin asked innocently. “She’s like my niece…did I Nigerian prince him? I did.” But Martin’s honesty didn’t appear to make Rosenberg feel any better about the spend. Especially for a product he didn’t really want. “I cannot believe you got me to spend $45 on godforsaken popcorn that I’m never gonna eat and it’s not your kid? This is such a violation!” Rosenberg ranted. Martin insisted it’s really good popcorn and urged Rosenberg to think about the kids and all the good his $45 or $50 can do for them. “I don’t give a damn about that Montessori school!” Rosenberg continued. “This isn’t for poor children, it’s for a Montessori school!” Now that Martin told the truth about the popcorn sale not being for her daughter, Rosenberg pressed her to tell the truth on whether she knew he was only buying popcorn because he believed it was for her daughter. “Yeah, that’s how scams work,” Martin admitted without any hesitation. “Did I run up and get everybody to donate to my beloved niece’s little popcorn drive situation? Rosenberg and Martin were on First Take Wednesday morning. And in the afternoon, Martin joined Rosenberg’s ESPN New York radio show with Don La Greca and Alan Hahn. During the radio appearance, Martin joked about Rosenberg being a “diva” on First Take earlier in the day, which prompted Rosenberg to accuse Martin of holding him up for $50. But even while accusing Martin of holding him up for $50, he didn’t realize he was being scammed by his ESPN colleague. Despite being longtime colleagues, Wednesday was the first time Rosenberg and Martin met in person. And upon meeting, Martin told Rosenberg about a popcorn fundraiser for her daughter. ﻿ “I did lie,” Martin admitted on the radio. “I said it was my child. item.title: See which 4 SouthCoast girls soccer teams qualified for the playoffs
item.description: Four of the SouthCoast’s nine high school girls soccer teams have qualified for the 2026 MIAA state tournament. Apponequet is seeded 26th in Div. 3 while Old Rochester is No. 30 in the same bracket. Dartmouth is the No. 35 seed in Div. 2 while Old Colony is seeded 26th in Div. 5. Apponequet, Old Colony and Old Rochester host preliminary round games while Dartmouth opens the tournament on the road. Here’s a look at the four local girls soccer teams and their opening matchups: Apponequet Record: 10-6-1 Seed: No. 26 in Div. 3 Opening matchup: Hosts No. 39 Marlborough (7-6-5) in the preliminary round at a date and time to be determined. Preview: See which 6 SouthCoast volleyball teams qualified for the playoffs Preview: See which 4 SouthCoast field hockey teams qualified for the playoffs Dartmouth Record: 8-6-2 Seed: No. 35 in Div. 2 Opening matchup: Visits No. 30 Nashoba Regional (6-10-2) in the preliminary round at a date and time to be determined. Old Colony Record: 7-10-1 Seed: No. 26 Div. 5 Opening matchup: Hosts No. 39 Mount Everett Regional (8-8-2) in the preliminary round at a date and time to be determined. Old Rochester Record: 9-7-1 Seed: No. 30 in Div. 3 Opening matchup: Hosts No. 35 Greater Lowell Tech (14-1-0) in the preliminary round at a date and time to be determined. item.title: D&D’s World of Warcraft Designer Hid a Personal Easter Egg in Plain Sight
item.description: Mounts in World of Warcraft are status symbols, a way of showing off the challenging raids you’ve completed or how far in the PvP ranks you’ve climbed. Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft lead designer James Wyatt couldn’t help showing off himself a bit in the book’s art, where he slipped in an image of his Night Elf warrior riding the Spirit of Eche'ro. Acquiring the spectral moose required spending hours digging up bone fragments with the Archaeology profession, an activity so tedious it was discontinued after the 2018 expansion Battle for Azeroth .

item.title: Hailee Steinfeld’s Brother Griffin Is a NASCAR-Bred Racer Building 2,000-HP Trucks
item.description: Hailee Steinfeld is known for the screen and the stage, but the horsepower in her family belongs to her older brother, Griffin Steinfeld. A former NASCAR driver, he now builds and drag races some of the wildest street-legal machines around, including a twin-turbo pickup that makes roughly 2,000 horsepower. From NASCAR to the Drag Strip Griffin was racing on the NASCAR circuit at 17 while still a senior at Westlake High School, then ran three seasons in the K&N Pro Series West, according to Motorious. He also raced off-road trucks and circle track before moving into drag racing and the radial-tire events at the heart of small-tire racing . He made his Radial vs. the World debut in the Miller family’s twin-turbo “Bumblebee” Camaro, has driven Jeff Miller’s 3.6-second car, and warmed up Antron Brown’s Top Fuel dragster at the Winternationals, Drag Illustrated reports. The Builds The headliner is his twin-turbo 1956 Chevy Apache pickup. It makes about 1,400 horsepower at 20 psi and roughly 2,000 at 40 psi, runs on radial tires, and is street-legal, with an estimated 0.8-second 0-60 mph time. It has run 4.60 seconds at 167 mph in the eighth mile. Griffin did much of the work himself, and his philosophy is simple: “Slicks are for slow cars.” A Rat Rod Jeff 1932 Ford rat rod build. Image via Autotopia LA/YouTube His newest project is a 1932 Ford rat rod from fabricator Rat Rod Jeff Jones, the builder behind the blown, 900-plus-horsepower rat rod we covered earlier . Dragzine reports it packs a 565-cubic-inch aluminum big-block Chevy with a supercharger reworked from Don Schumacher Racing’s Top Fuel program. It currently makes low 900s horsepower at the tire, and Griffin says pulley changes could push it to about 1,700. The build took 10 months from the ground up, starting with a half-buried 1932 Ford body Jones dug up on his property. Griffin found Jones on Instagram and got weekly photo updates, and his logo is hand-rolled into the wheel tubs. The car has no track passes yet. Griffin credits his father, Peter Steinfeld, with part of the spark: “My dad and I always loved rat rods.” Another look at a Rat Rod Jeff build. Image via Autotopia LA/YouTube Where Hailee Comes In The two worlds crossed on the set of Bumblebee (2018). Griffin was there with his sister when the production needed someone to drive the film’s Volkswagen Beetle for a time-sensitive scene, and he got the stunt job. It was a fitting assignment for a car that has long been a pop culture icon . He later met the Miller family after spotting their Bumblebee-themed Camaro at a South Carolina movie theater promotion. What’s Next Griffin has said he wants to race in the NHRA, with Pro Mod, Top Alcohol Dragster, or Top Fuel on his radar, depending on funding. Celebrity gearheads are having a moment, from Sydney Sweeney’s ’65 Mustang and Syd’s Garage trademark to the Steinfeld garage, and Griffin’s rat rod hasn’t even made its first pass yet. Featured image: collage using a photo of Hailee Stein

item.title: EA is bringing 25 classic PC games to Steam
item.description: This Road Rash screenshot rules. Electronic Arts is launching 25 classic games on Steam, including "Anniversary Editions" of the motorcycle racer Road Rash and six Wing Commander titles. These Anniversary Editions preserve "the original look, feel and creative intent of the game" but also have quality-of-life updates to support modern systems and controls and improve performance, according to EA . The seven new editions were "inspired" by the discovery of a "physical media vault" with "thousands" of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes and "other media assets," EA says. As part of the digitization process, EA was able to recover master FMV sequences and reedited them to restore more … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Get root on a musl Linux system by slamming it with an overly long password
item.description: On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions. The flaw affects certain Linux systems using musl libc instead of the traditional GNU C library, and even then only those running OpenSSH's secure shell daemon without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) and with password authentication enabled. If those conditions are met, and at least one other account has a valid password hash, accounts that shouldn't accept passwords, such as root, key-only deployment users, and LDAP users, may be accessed by supplying a password between 257 and 1,024 characters. The targeted accounts must have an asterisk (*) in their password field, and direct root login remains subject to OpenSSH's configuration. That might seem niche, but sorry: It’s not. Musl libc is common in embedded Linux systems due to its low footprint. More critically than that, it's also the standard C library for Alpine Linux, which provides official cloud images for both AWS and Azure. Some Alpine systems running in those environments may therefore be vulnerable, depending on their configuration. Dawn of the *sshole The vulnerability in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems dates back to 2016, but Kültekin explains that its roots go back much further – to the BSD Unix era, actually. In 1980, Sun Microsystems cofounder and BSD Unix heavyweight Bill Joy was involved in the development of BSD Unix, whose password file contained a single asterisk in the /etc/passwd entry for the daemon user. The asterisk wasn't a password hash and effectively disabled password authentication for that account. Nowadays, password hashes typically live in /etc/shadow and contain hashed information that the system uses to verify a plaintext password entered by a user. Asterisks are still present for accounts that aren't supposed to accept password logins, but as Kültekin explains in his writeup, that isn't exactly a foolproof way to keep people out. The crypt() function, which generates password hashes for comparison with stored values, can return NULL if it can't compute a hash. Applications that fail to check that result may crash. Musl libc's developers instead chose to return a single character for certain failures, and they picked the asterisk. Musl also added SHA-512-based password hashing around the same time, which Kültekin notes gets slower the longer a password is, potentially leading to denial of service if someone floods a server with a super-long password. Musl capped passwords at 256 bytes, and you can likely see where this is going. In 2016, OpenSSH introduced a workaround to prevent attackers from enumerating valid account names through SSH. Before the change, sshd could reject authentication attempts for nonexistent users more quickly than those for valid accounts. Attempts against valid accounts took long
item.dc:creator: Brandon Vigliarolo
item.content:encoded: On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions. The flaw affects certain Linux systems using musl libc instead of the traditional GNU C library, and even then only those running OpenSSH's secure shell daemon without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) and with password authentication enabled. If those conditions are met, and at least one other account has a valid password hash, accounts that shouldn't accept passwords, such as root, key-only deployment users, and LDAP users, may be accessed by supplying a password between 257 and 1,024 characters. The targeted accounts must have an asterisk (*) in their password field, and direct root login remains subject to OpenSSH's configuration. That might seem niche, but sorry: It’s not. Musl libc is common in embedded Linux systems due to its low footprint. More critically than that, it's also the standard C library for Alpine Linux, which provides official cloud images for both AWS and Azure. Some Alpine systems running in those environments may therefore be vulnerable, depending on their configuration. Dawn of the *sshole The vulnerability in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems dates back to 2016, but Kültekin explains that its roots go back much further – to the BSD Unix era, actually. In 1980, Sun Microsystems cofounder and BSD Unix heavyweight Bill Joy was involved in the development of BSD Unix, whose password file contained a single asterisk in the /etc/passwd entry for the daemon user. The asterisk wasn't a password hash and effectively disabled password authentication for that account. Nowadays, password hashes typically live in /etc/shadow and contain hashed information that the system uses to verify a plaintext password entered by a user. Asterisks are still present for accounts that aren't supposed to accept password logins, but as Kültekin explains in his writeup, that isn't exactly a foolproof way to keep people out. The crypt() function, which generates password hashes for comparison with stored values, can return NULL if it can't compute a hash. Applications that fail to check that result may crash. Musl libc's developers instead chose to return a single character for certain failures, and they picked the asterisk. Musl also added SHA-512-based password hashing around the same time, which Kültekin notes gets slower the longer a password is, potentially leading to denial of service if someone floods a server with a super-long password. Musl capped passwords at 256 bytes, and you can likely see where this is going. In 2016, OpenSSH introduced a workaround to prevent attackers from enumerating valid account names through SSH. Before the change, sshd could reject authentication attempts for nonexistent users more quickly than those for valid accounts. Attempts against valid accounts took longer because the server had to hash the supplied password before rejecting it. The solution was to have sshd perform dummy password hashing for invalid users, using an appropriate hashing algorithm and salt to reduce differences in response times. On affected musl-based Linux systems, accounts marked with an asterisk instead of a password hash could be busted open by supplying a password longer than 256 bytes – a flaw dating back to 2016. Any musl-based Linux system running a vulnerable OpenSSH configuration without PAM, with password authentication enabled, at least one account marked with an asterisk, and another account with a valid password hash could be vulnerable to a *sshole attack. Luckily, OpenSSH acted fast to fix this issue , and any OpenSSH build 10.6p2 (released Thursday) or newer is protected. Alternatively, if you can’t update your OpenSSH implementation on an affected system, just disable password authentication and restart the SSH daemon and you should be all set. There’s no indication that vulnerable systems have been exploited, but if you want to check, Kültekin has included a simple CLI command in his writeup that can be used to check if any no-password accounts on a sensitive machine recently took a password. ®

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Almathea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water'
item.description: null On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists. The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft. The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong. However, NASA quickly fixed the problem and got Galileo working again. Less than a year later, Galileo threw itself into Jupiter's atmosphere . The spacecraft was crushed by the high pressure in Jupiter's atmosphere, but its data still survives on Earth. The Jupiter moon Amalthea as seen by NASA's Galileo spacecraft on Nov. 5, 2002. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Why it mattered The Galileo spacecraft was running on cosmic fumes by the time it reached Amalthea and the flyby would be the last time the probe would ever swing by one of Jupiter's moons . While it may not look like it in Galileo's black and white images above and below, Amalthea is tinted red due sulfur contamination on its surface. The moon is small, about 168 miles long, and orbits about 112,468 miles (181,000 km) from Jupiter (much closer to the planet than the Earth and its moon). Galileo flew within 99 miles of Amalthea during its flyby, which also marked the closest Galileo would get to Jupiter before its death dive in September 2005. "Scientists studying data from NASA's Galileo spacecraft have found that Jupiter's moon Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble less dense than water," NASA announced in May 2005 Two views of the Jupiter moon Amalthea as seen by NASA's Galileo spacecraft. NASA/JPL-Caltech These images of Jupiter's moon Amalthea were taken with NASA's Galileo and Voyager spacecraft. Galileo's image is on the right, with Voyager's view on the left. The center image is a composite of both probes. NASA/JPL-Caltech "Amalthea is throwing us a curve ball," Torrence Johnson, a study co-author on the Almathea flyby and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, said in 2005 . "Its density is well below that of water ice, and even with substantial porosity, Amalthea probably contains a lot of water ice, as well as rock." Originally known as Jupiter V (because it was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the so-called Galilean moons Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto ), Amalthea was named after naiad, or water nymph, from Greek mythology. It is fitting that Amalthea was the last of Jupiter's moons to be visited by the Galileo spacecraft. The moon was also last Jupiter moon to be discovered by visual observation
item.dc:creator: Hanneke Weitering

While it may not look like it in Galileo's black and white images above and below, Amalthea is tinted red due sulfur contamination on its surface. The moon is small, about 168 miles long, and orbits about 112,468 miles (181,000 km) from Jupiter (much closer to the planet than the Earth and its moon). Galileo flew within 99 miles of Amalthea during its flyby, which also marked the closest Galileo would get to Jupiter before its death dive in September 2005. "Scientists studying data from NASA's Galileo spacecraft have found that Jupiter's moon Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble less dense than water," NASA announced in May 2005 Two views of the Jupiter moon Amalthea as seen by NASA's Galileo spacecraft. NASA/JPL-Caltech These images of Jupiter's moon Amalthea were taken with NASA's Galileo and Voyager spacecraft. Galileo's image is on the right, with Voyager's view on the left. The center image is a composite of both probes. NASA/JPL-Caltech "Amalthea is throwing us a curve ball," Torrence Johnson, a study co-author on the Almathea flyby and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, said in 2005 . "Its density is well below that of water ice, and even with substantial porosity, Amalthea probably contains a lot of water ice, as well as rock." Originally known as Jupiter V (because it was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the so-called Galilean moons Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto ), Amalthea was named after naiad, or water nymph, from Greek mythology. It is fitting that Amalthea was the last of Jupiter's moons to be visited by the Galileo spacecraft. The moon was also last Jupiter moon to be discovered by visual observations when it was first disovered by astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard in September 1892 using the Lick Observatory telescope in California. The Galileo spacecraft ultimately crashed into Jupiter on Sept. 21, 2005, less than a year after its Amalthea flyby. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: How to change the time of day in Zelda Ocarina of Time
item.description: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , you need to change the time of day to complete certain missions. The people of Hyrule are living their lives while Link is trying to save the world. As a result, the availability of places and characters change depending on the time of the day. You might need to wait until nighttime to finish a quest or only find an NPC to talk to when the sun is shinning brightly.

item.title: Headliners Announced For NECLive 2026
item.description: NECLive , the Nigerian Entertainment Conference, today announced the first confirmed lineup for its 11th edition. The lineup brings together award-winning actors, filmmakers, music executives, entrepreneurs and award-winning DJs. The three-day annual conference takes place in November with a flagship event on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at Alliance Française de Lagos, Ikoyi. This year’s show is presented under the theme “Home Advantage: Transforming Local Demand into Global Power.” Comedian and compere Tee A returns as host, extending his record as NECLive’s resident host and committee member. He will be joined by multiple co-hosts, moderators and interviewers, all to be confirmed later. For the first time, we now unveil the confirmed participants for 2026. Across Film and Television, the lineup features Inkblot Studio founder Naz Onuzo , actors Genoveva Umeh , Omowunmi Dada , Chimezie Imo , Uzoamaka Power , Efa Iwara , and Charles Born , directors Kayode Kasum and Dika Ofoma , creator Tobe Ugeh and PR expert Jennifer Ukoh-Osamwonyi , alongside key industry voices. The Business of Music and fashion section brings together managing directors Godwin Tom and Foza Fawehinmi , senior manager Excel Joab , music executive Bizzle Osikoya , fashion stylist The Style Infidel and talent manager Femisoro Ajayi . Representing Sound and Culture are DJ Obi , singer Greatman Takit, head of Energize Music Dr. Foy , co-founder Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi , and managing partner Tobi Mohammed . Driving Business and Leadership are regional managers Njideka Akabogu and Iretomiwa Akintunde-Johnson , CEO Oluwaseye Oladejo , Founder TSC Agency Ozinna Anumudu, Founder Big Tech This Week Fatu Ogwuche and head of AI Labs Joseph Enesu . “ Nigeria’s creative industries already have the audience. The work now is turning that demand into lasting value at home and abroad. Everyone in this first lineup has done that in their own field, from the AMVCAs to Netflix, Sony and a Monday night in Lagos,” said Ayeni Adekunle , Convener of NECLive. NECLive is presented by ID Africa and Netng in partnership with Plaqad, the African artificial intelligence and business solutions company, The Macallan, MTN Nigeria Communications PLC, BHM and Huce Valeris. BellaNaija is a Media Partner for NECLive The post Headliners Announced For NECLive 2026 appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.description: By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP. While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu , declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party. The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought. The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State. Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP. While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu , declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party. The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought. The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State. Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. Rejecting attempts to portray his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries. “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said. Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said. On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025. He said the court had dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership after upholding objections bordering on jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, adding that the substantive issues were also resolved in favour of the defendants. “Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal,” he said. The former Vice-President urged ADC supporters to remain peaceful and law-abiding, insisting that the ruling would not interrupt the party’s mobilisation. “Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said. With the campaign train already in Kebbi, Atiku urged supporters to take the party’s message from house to house and door to door, declaring, “There is no shaking.” Obi warns against undermining democracy Also reacting to the development, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. Obi, who expressed shock over the judgment, said the development had created uncertainty in the country’s political landscape, particularly with the 2027 general election approaching. He disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Thursday. The former Anambra State governor said although he respected the court’s authority to determine disputes in accordance with the law, the timing of the judgment raised concerns about electoral certainty. “I do not challenge the ruling of the court. The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty,” he said. Obi argued that uncertainty over political parties and their candidates close to an election could undermine the electoral process and restrict the space for opposition campaigns. He alleged that the ruling party was engineering instability within opposition parties, claiming that similar developments had affected him in the Labour Party. He also alleged that opposition campaigns had been subjected to violence, describing the developments as part of what he called efforts to shrink the civic space and weaken opposition politics. Emphasising the importance of voters in a democracy, Obi said the choice of political leaders should ultimately rest with the electorate. “One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders. I trust in the judiciary. As a public officer, I have shown deep respect for the judiciary,” he said. He appealed to the judiciary and other stakeholders to protect democratic institutions and ensure that candidates were allowed to participate freely in electoral contests. Obi further warned against weakening opposition politics, citing the spread of military rule in parts of West Africa as a reason Nigeria should strengthen its democratic institutions. According to him, the survival of democracy requires a political environment in which opposition parties are allowed to operate, organise and compete without persecution. He said he had consistently maintained that, if elected president, he would give special attention to ensuring that opposition parties remained stable and viable. Obi added that his administration would protect opposition candidates from being pushed out of electoral contests. “This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said. item.title: October crypto-tracker hack: Access cracked, law enforcement tokens packed
item.description: Blockchain analysis outfit Chainalysis has confirmed that when attackers broke into its systems in October, they managed to grab usernames, password hashes, and live tokens. In an update written late Wednesday evening, the company, a leader in blockchain analysis which has some very high-profile global customers and partners, confirmed the impact of the attack for the first time. In previous updates, which Chainalysis has issued regularly since it detected the intrusion on October 30, it confirmed that user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organizational role labels were exposed. The news of password hashes and live tokens also being accessed reflects a worsening picture for the company. Chainalysis did not confirm the type of hashing algorithm it used to encrypt users' passwords, which makes it difficult to draw conclusions about the offline crackability of users' hashed credentials. Some users received emails instructing them to change their passwords, but Chainalysis said in its latest update that the password reset functionality is currently down. Nevertheless, users were also encouraged to change their passwords on any site where they reuse credentials. In addition to the exposed data, Chainalysis also detected "abnormal activity" on its transaction screening products, and has taken services down while "our team completes critical work." These include, but are not limited to, the Reactor blockchain investigation platform used by international law enforcement customers, the Data Solutions threat intelligence platform, and the KYT (know your transaction) anti-money laundering solution's user interface and login page. Regarding Reactor and the associated investigation data, Chainalysis said : "At this time, we continue to have no evidence that any investigations data has been accessed or Chainalysis attribution data has been manipulated." The company plans to reinstate KYT and the risk-intelligence Address Screening tool at some point today (Thursday November 5). Customers will have to provide the company’s support team or their account manager with trusted IP addresses, which will be added to an allowlist. From there, users can begin resetting their passwords . "We are working around the clock to harden our systems and bring Reactor and Data Solutions back online," Chainalysis said. "We will require additional protections to access accounts, including that every user will have to reset passwords and rotate API keys as appropriate. We will communicate these changes as necessary. "We know how business-critical these services are to our customers, and we are working expeditiously alongside our outside experts to restore them securely." Chainalysis has not yet commented on who was behind the attack, but implied that the culprits used an AI agent, and likened the attack to others that have hit "many other tech platforms in recent weeks." item.dc:creator: Connor Jones
item.content:encoded: Blockchain analysis outfit Chainalysis has confirmed that when attackers broke into its systems in October, they managed to grab usernames, password hashes, and live tokens. In an update written late Wednesday evening, the company, a leader in blockchain analysis which has some very high-profile global customers and partners, confirmed the impact of the attack for the first time. In previous updates, which Chainalysis has issued regularly since it detected the intrusion on October 30, it confirmed that user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organizational role labels were exposed. The news of password hashes and live tokens also being accessed reflects a worsening picture for the company. Chainalysis did not confirm the type of hashing algorithm it used to encrypt users' passwords, which makes it difficult to draw conclusions about the offline crackability of users' hashed credentials. Some users received emails instructing them to change their passwords, but Chainalysis said in its latest update that the password reset functionality is currently down. Nevertheless, users were also encouraged to change their passwords on any site where they reuse credentials. In addition to the exposed data, Chainalysis also detected "abnormal activity" on its transaction screening products, and has taken services down while "our team completes critical work." These include, but are not limited to, the Reactor blockchain investigation platform used by international law enforcement customers, the Data Solutions threat intelligence platform, and the KYT (know your transaction) anti-money laundering solution's user interface and login page. Regarding Reactor and the associated investigation data, Chainalysis said : "At this time, we continue to have no evidence that any investigations data has been accessed or Chainalysis attribution data has been manipulated." The company plans to reinstate KYT and the risk-intelligence Address Screening tool at some point today (Thursday November 5). Customers will have to provide the company’s support team or their account manager with trusted IP addresses, which will be added to an allowlist. From there, users can begin resetting their passwords . "We are working around the clock to harden our systems and bring Reactor and Data Solutions back online," Chainalysis said. "We will require additional protections to access accounts, including that every user will have to reset passwords and rotate API keys as appropriate. We will communicate these changes as necessary. "We know how business-critical these services are to our customers, and we are working expeditiously alongside our outside experts to restore them securely." Chainalysis has not yet commented on who was behind the attack, but implied that the culprits used an AI agent, and likened the attack to others that have hit "many other tech platforms in recent weeks." "This month, Chainalysis detected an external actor using offensive agentic techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools," it told customers in its initial disclosure on October 30. "Our teams have been working around the clock to investigate unauthorized activity, patch vulnerabilities, and harden our systems." In Wednesday's updates, it referred to the intrusion as an "ongoing multifront cyberattack," and later, an "on-path attack," otherwise known as an attacker-in-the-middle (AitM) attack, without elaborating further about what it entailed. Per its own company description, Chainalysis counts government agencies, cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions, and cybersecurity companies among its customer base. It is one of the world's foremost blockchain analysis companies and is routinely engaged to assist in cyber-related law enforcement investigations. Recent cases the company was asked to support include the takedowns of crypto-laundering network AudiA6 and bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine, both of which were known facilitators of ransomware crews. It also played a role in bringing down the infamous LockBit ransomware operation, among other engagements in the interim. ®

item.title: No child is useless, every child is ordained for greatness — Foluke Adeboye
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The wife of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Foluke Adeboye, has called on parents, churches, governments and other stakeholders to take greater responsibility for raising children with godly character and values, saying Nigeria’s future depends on how its young people are nurtured. Adeboye made the call in her welcome address, titled “The Mandate of Kingdom Education in National Transformation,” at the annual summit of Christ The Redeemer’s School Management (CRSM), a multidimensional ministry of the RCCG, held at Redemption City of God along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The summit was themed “Revisiting Kingdom Education: The Role of Stakeholders.” She said the responsibility for effective Christian education begins at home, urging parents to train their children properly and cooperate with teachers in shaping their character. Adeboye cautioned parents against over-pampering their children during school holidays, urging them to allow the young ones to grow in accordance with godly values. “Every child must fear God because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. We see many of these children that look down on their teachers. If parents discharge their duties effectively, it will make the teacher’s work easier. Meditate on God’s word day and night,” she said. She also urged parents not to shy away from correcting their children, stressing that discipline and proper upbringing were essential to national development. “If only everyone of us can come together, do the right things, raise our children rightly, the success of Nigeria is in our hands,” she added. Adeboye further charged children to obey their parents and called on churches to teach sound biblical doctrines. She urged leaders to discharge their responsibilities diligently and exercise sound judgment, warning that failure to provide responsible leadership could create room for corruption, criminality and other social vices. On the role of government, she called for the provision of adequate structures and learning facilities in schools, particularly in rural communities where, she said, some pupils still sit on the floor because of a lack of chairs. She noted that such schools were often upgraded through evangelism and missionary activities because of the need to address the challenges confronting rural education. “So many things are wrong and these children from the village have great destiny to fulfil. God is counting on them. They brought David from the bush to be a king of Israel. No child is a useless child; God ordained every child to be great. I believe by the time I leave, I must have made substantial impact over the education in this nation,” she said. In her keynote address on the same topic, former Minister of Education, Dr Oby Ezekwesili, said professionals who remained indifferent to the challenges facing society could not contribute meaningfully to its transformation. Adeboye cautioned parents against over-pampering their children during school holidays, urging them to allow the young ones to grow in accordance with godly values. “Every child must fear God because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. God is counting on them. They brought David from the bush to be a king of Israel. No child is a useless child; God ordained every child to be great. I believe by the time I leave, I must have made substantial impact over the education in this nation,” she said. In her keynote address on the same topic, former Minister of Education, Dr Oby Ezekwesili, said professionals who remained indifferent to the challenges facing society could not contribute meaningfully to its transformation. Ezekwesili expressed concern over Nigeria’s education challenges, particularly the high number of out-of-school children, and urged Christians to demonstrate the values they profess, noting that they were called to be the light of the world. She said nation-building required children equipped with character, competence and capacity, describing the three qualities as essential to preparing young people for responsible citizenship. According to her, Christian schools must promote diligence, courage, compassion and stewardship as core values, describing the approach as character-based education. The panelists also stressed that Kingdom Education should produce ethical citizens who actively contribute to society rather than remain passive spectators. They said school activities, including curriculum delivery, should be anchored on a biblical worldview, adding that Kingdom schools must prepare students to understand their identity, defend their faith and withstand social pressure. item.title: Tinubu saved Nigeria from turning to Venezuela — Emerhor
item.description: A founding leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor, has declared that Nigeria would have suffered an economic collapse similar to Venezuela’s if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not demonstrated the courage and foresight to introduce far-reaching economic reforms upon assuming office in 2023. Olorogun Emerhor, who stated this on Thursday during the Delta State APC campaign flag-off in Oleh, Isoko South Local Government Area, said Tinubu inherited an economy weakened by years of poor management and unsustainable policies, insisting that the President’s difficult but necessary decisions had rescued the country from the brink of economic disaster. The APC chieftain also called for the re-election of President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in 2027, arguing that both leaders had demonstrated the capacity to reposition the country and state for sustainable economic growth and infrastructural transformation. According to Emerhor, Nigeria was heading towards an economic crisis comparable to that of Venezuela, an oil-rich South American country that experienced severe economic difficulties despite possessing some of the world’s largest crude oil reserves. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rescued Nigeria. If our President had not taken those bold decisions, Nigeria would have gone the way of Venezuela. Do you want Nigeria to become another Venezuela? “Venezuela has more oil than Nigeria, but bad leadership and years of economic mismanagement destroyed its economy. For many years, that was the kind of governance we experienced in Nigeria,” he stated. Emerhor criticised some opposition political figures seeking to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that several of them were part of the political establishment responsible for the country’s longstanding economic difficulties. He maintained that it took Tinubu’s political courage and determination to confront the structural challenges that previous administrations had failed to address. “All those who are today running to become President were part of the system that contributed to the destruction of Nigeria. It was Bola Ahmed Tinubu who had the courage to take those difficult decisions. “Today, we are beginning to have a stable economy. The President has laid a strong foundation for economic prosperity. We have a prudent President, and our foreign reserves are growing. Tinubu is doing well,” Emerhor declared. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: A founding leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor, has declared that Nigeria would have suffered an economic collapse similar to Venezuela’s if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not demonstrated the courage and foresight to introduce far-reaching economic reforms upon assuming office in 2023. Olorogun Emerhor, who stated this on Thursday during the Delta State APC campaign flag-off in Oleh, Isoko South Local Government Area, said Tinubu inherited an economy weakened by years of poor management and unsustainable policies, insisting that the President’s difficult but necessary decisions had rescued the country from the brink of economic disaster. The APC chieftain also called for the re-election of President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in 2027, arguing that both leaders had demonstrated the capacity to reposition the country and state for sustainable economic growth and infrastructural transformation. According to Emerhor, Nigeria was heading towards an economic crisis comparable to that of Venezuela, an oil-rich South American country that experienced severe economic difficulties despite possessing some of the world’s largest crude oil reserves. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rescued Nigeria. If our President had not taken those bold decisions, Nigeria would have gone the way of Venezuela. Do you want Nigeria to become another Venezuela? “Venezuela has more oil than Nigeria, but bad leadership and years of economic mismanagement destroyed its economy. For many years, that was the kind of governance we experienced in Nigeria,” he stated. Emerhor criticised some opposition political figures seeking to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that several of them were part of the political establishment responsible for the country’s longstanding economic difficulties. He maintained that it took Tinubu’s political courage and determination to confront the structural challenges that previous administrations had failed to address. “All those who are today running to become President were part of the system that contributed to the destruction of Nigeria. It was Bola Ahmed Tinubu who had the courage to take those difficult decisions. “Today, we are beginning to have a stable economy. The President has laid a strong foundation for economic prosperity. We have a prudent President, and our foreign reserves are growing. Tinubu is doing well,” Emerhor declared. The APC leader argued that removing Tinubu after his first term would amount to abandoning the economic recovery process midway, stressing that the President deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms and deliver their anticipated benefits to Nigerians. Using the analogy of constructing a building, Emerhor said the President had successfully laid the foundation for Nigeria’s economic recovery and should be allowed to complete the structure. “Do you want to invite those who destroyed the house to come back and rebuild it? We have to give President Tinubu another four years to build the skyscraper on top of the foundation he has laid. “We need to give him those four years, and you will see what Nigeria will become. We must give him our full support,” he said. Turning to Delta State, Emerhor showered praises on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, describing his performance under the MORE Agenda as remarkable and deserving of another term in office. He said the governor had recorded significant achievements in infrastructure and other critical sectors within barely three and a half years, expressing confidence that another four years would position Delta State among Nigeria’s most developed states. Emerhor, who referred to Oborevwori by his popular nickname, Ukodo, said the governor’s achievements were so numerous that recounting them would be like singing the popular Christian hymn, Count Your Blessings. “Now, let me talk about our Ukodo. Many people have already counted so many things that he has done. I would have loved us to sing, ‘Count your blessings, name them one by one.’ “Look at what he has done in just three years. Give him another four years, and we will beat Lagos. Don’t you want that?” he asked, drawing cheers from party supporters. The APC founding leader further declared that the massive gathering of political leaders and supporters at the Oleh campaign flag-off demonstrated the growing strength and dominance of the ruling party in Delta State. He described the occasion as a gathering of the state’s political heavyweights, insisting that the APC had emerged as the dominant political force ahead of the 2027 general elections. “I have come here today as the happiest man. I can see the cream of the political class, all the political juggernauts, gathered here today. “There is no other party in Delta State than APC! Anybody pretending that there is another party in this state is deceiving himself. Can you see what is happening here today?” he declared. Emerhor maintained that the unity of political leaders and the massive turnout of supporters at the campaign flag-off were indications of the party’s strength and electoral prospects. He urged party members not to become complacent but to translate the enthusiasm witnessed at the rally into effective grassroots mobilisation and votes during the elections. Addressing the crowd, which he estimated at more than 20,000 people, Emerhor challenged every supporter to mobilise at least ten additional voters for President Tinubu and other APC candidates. “The people in this stadium are more than 20,000. Every one of you should go back and make sure you get a minimum of ten people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “If everybody here brings ten additional voters, imagine the number of votes we will deliver. We have already won the election,” he declared. Emerhor expressed confidence that the combination of Tinubu’s economic reforms, Oborevwori’s infrastructural achievements and the unity of APC stakeholders would strengthen the party’s chances of securing overwhelming electoral victories in Delta State. He urged party faithful to sustain their commitment to grassroots mobilisation, stressing that the 2027 elections would provide an opportunity for Nigerians and Deltans to consolidate what he described as the gains of purposeful leadership at the federal and state levels. item.title: ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has criticised the court ruling nullifying the African Democratic Congress (ADC) executive committee and its candidates, alleging that the development could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in Nigeria. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties. CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state. The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation. The statement read in part: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.” It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process. CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system. The coalition warned that the judiciary must remain guided by the Constitution and the interests of Nigerians rather than political considerations. “The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement said. CUPP declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism. The coalition added: “CUPP stands in solidarity with the ADC and all progressive forces in Nigeria. We will not sit idly by while the hard-earned democratic gains of our nation are plundered by an authoritarian regime.” The post ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mass Effect Studio’s Closure Is Getting Its Own Movie
item.description: Electronic Arts delivered a brutal blow to the video game industry a few weeks ago when it finally closed the legendary RPG studio BioWare . The team created Mass Effect , Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , and many other classics. After a wave of mourning across the industry , a recent Bloomberg report claimed that EA shut down the studio, so the publisher could focus its resources on Star Wars Battlefront 3 instead of a rival sci-fi title in a new Mass Effect. It seems that we’ll soon know more details about what exactly went down.

item.title: PSC posts four commissioners of police to states
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of four Commissioners of Police to Plateau, Enugu, Nasarawa and Ondo states following interviews to assess their suitability for the new assignments. The commission’s spokesman, Torty Njoku, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday at the Solomon Arase Conference Hall, PSC headquarters, Abuja. The newly posted commissioners are CP Sunday J. A. Okoebor, formerly Commissioner of Police, Police Accounts and Budget, Force Headquarters, who has been posted to Plateau State. Others are CP Fidelis Ogarabe, formerly Commissioner of Police, INTERPOL Annex, Lagos, posted to Enugu State; CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, formerly Commissioner of Police, Force Intelligence Annex, Lagos, posted to Nasarawa State; and CP Johnson Ayodeji Babalola, formerly Commissioner of Police, Special Inquiry, Force Headquarters, Abuja, posted to Ondo State. The Chairman of the commission, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu, who affirmed the postings, said they were in line with Section 215(1)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which empowers the commission to appoint Commissioners of Police for each state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory. Argungu, who was represented by a board member, Hon. Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC rtd.), said the officers had demonstrated the requisite knowledge and character during the interviews. He urged them to discharge their responsibilities with impartiality and live up to the expectations of their new offices. The post PSC posts four commissioners of police to states appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France needs 'more public services', 'salaries are too low', 'schools are in very, very bad shape'
item.description: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”

Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”

item.title: Concacaf revamps Gold Cup format to make tournament ‘more competitive’
item.description: Group stage to involve two groups of eight teams Change resembles model of Uefa Champions League Concacaf on Thursday announced changes to the format of the Gold Cup, the confederation’s regional championship. The move is aimed at “delivering more meaningful matches and matchups between top-ranked teams”, Concacaf said in a statement. Once the primary focus of teams in the region, the 35-year-old tournament will return for its 19th edition in 2027 having lost a bit of luster. The federation’s tweaks to the format – which center around the competition’s group stage – could help restore that. Here’s a look at the tournament, what’s at stake and what is changing.
